title.zh: 卷二百八十 列傳第三十九 田紹斌 王榮 楊瓊 錢守俊 徐興 王杲 李重誨 白守素 張思鈞 李琪 王延範
title.en: Volume 280 Biographies 39: Tian Shaobin, Wang Rong, Yang Qiong, Qian Shoujun, Xu Xing, Wang Gao, Li Zhonghui, Bai Shousu, Zhang Sijun, Li Qi, Wang Yanfan
title.raw: 卷二百八十 列傳第三十九 田紹斌 王榮 楊瓊 錢守俊 徐興 王杲 李重誨 白守素 張思鈞 李琪 王延範 Volume 280 Biographies 39: Tian Shaobin, Wang Rong, Yang Qiong, Qian Shoujun, Xu Xing, Wang Gao, Li Zhonghui, Bai Shousu, Zhang Sijun, Li Qi, Wang Yanfan

sentences.zh: 田紹斌

translations.literal: Tian Shaobin
translations.idiomatic: Tian Shaobin

sentences.zh: 田紹斌，汾州人。

translations.literal: Tian Shaobin was a native of Fenzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Tian Shaobin was from Fenzhou.

sentences.zh: 仕河東劉鈞為佐聖軍使，戍遼州。

translations.literal: He served Liu Jun of Hedong as an assistant commander of the Zuosheng Army and was garrisoned at Liaozhou.
translations.idiomatic: He entered the service of Liu Jun of Hedong as deputy commander of the Zuosheng Army and was posted to garrison Liaozhou.

sentences.zh: 周顯德四年，領五十騎來歸，鈞屠其父母家屬。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Xiande of Zhou, he led fifty horsemen to come over in submission; Jun slaughtered his parents and family.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Xiande under the Later Zhou (957), he defected with fifty horsemen; Liu Jun had his parents and entire household put to death.

sentences.zh: 世宗召補驍武副指揮使。

translations.literal: Emperor Shizong summoned him and appointed him deputy commander of the Xiaowu [Valiant Martial] command.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shizong of Zhou summoned him and made him deputy commander of the Valiant Martial Guard.

sentences.zh: 宋初，隨崔彥進征李筠，攻大會砦，破之，以功遷龍捷指揮使。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Song, he followed Cui Yanjin in the campaign against Li Jun, attacked the Great Assembly stockade, broke it, and for his merit was promoted to commander of the Longjie [Dragon Swift] command.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Song, he marched with Cui Yanjin against Li Jun, stormed the Great Assembly stockade and took it, and was promoted to commander of the Dragon Swift Guard for his service.

sentences.zh: 又敗筠於澤州茶碾村，筠退保澤州，紹斌鑿濠圍守，流矢中左目，前軍部署韓令坤以其事聞。

translations.literal: He again defeated Jun at Chanian Village in Zezhou; Jun withdrew to hold Zezhou. Shaobin dug moats and besieged him; a stray arrow struck his left eye. The forward army deployer Han Lingkun reported the matter.
translations.idiomatic: He routed Li Jun again at Chanian Village in Zezhou; when Jun fell back to defend Zezhou itself, Shaobin dug trenches and laid siege. A stray arrow struck his left eye, and the forward commander Han Lingkun reported the incident to court.

sentences.zh: 及太祖召見於潞州，紹斌殺晉軍益眾，奪其鎧甲。

translations.literal: When the Taizu summoned him for audience at Luzhou, Shaobin killed ever more Jin troops and seized their armor.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizu summoned him to an audience at Luzhou, Shaobin went on killing Jin soldiers in ever greater numbers and stripping them of their armor.

sentences.zh: 又從討李重進於揚州，壁城南，圍三日，城潰，斬首踰千級。

translations.literal: He again followed in the punitive campaign against Li Chongjin at Yangzhou, encamped south of the wall, besieged for three days until the city collapsed, and beheaded more than a thousand.
translations.idiomatic: He also took part in the campaign against Li Chongjin at Yangzhou, camped south of the city walls, and after a three-day siege broke the defenses, taking more than a thousand heads.

sentences.zh: 賜袍帶、緡帛，尋補馬軍副都軍頭、龍衛指揮使。

translations.literal: He was granted robe, belt, and silk cash; shortly afterward he was appointed deputy commander-in-chief of the horse army and commander of the Longwei [Dragon Guard] command.
translations.idiomatic: He received robes, a belt, and silk stipends, and was soon made deputy commander-in-chief of the Cavalry Army and commander of the Dragon Guard.

sentences.zh: 下荊湖，平嶺南，率皆從行。

translations.literal: In the reduction of Jinghu and the pacification of Lingnan, he generally followed on these campaigns.
translations.idiomatic: He marched on nearly every major campaign of the early reign, including the conquest of Jinghu and the pacification of Lingnan.

sentences.zh: 討蜀，隸大將劉延讓麾下。

translations.literal: In the Shu expedition he was placed under the great general Liu Yanrang.
translations.idiomatic: During the Shu campaign he served under the senior commander Liu Yanrang.

sentences.zh: 會全師雄寇神泉，紹斌率所部敗其黨數千，時漢、劍道梗，因賴以寧，太祖遣使孫晏齎詔賜賚有加。

translations.literal: When Quan Shixiong raided Shenquan, Shaobin led his command and defeated several thousand of his followers. At the time the Han and Jian routes were blocked, and on this account the region came to rely on him for peace. Taizu sent the envoy Sun Yan bearing an edict with added rewards.
translations.idiomatic: When Quan Shixiong attacked Shenquan, Shaobin led his troops and routed several thousand of the rebel band. With the Han and Jian routes cut off, the region depended on him to restore order; Taizu sent the envoy Sun Yan with an edict and extra rewards.

sentences.zh: 凡在蜀三歲，剽盜殄除。

translations.literal: Altogether he was in Shu three years, and banditry was exterminated.
translations.idiomatic: He spent three years in Shu in all, during which brigandage was wiped out.

sentences.zh: 還，改龍捷都虞候。

translations.literal: On his return he was transferred to chief adjutant of the Longjie command.
translations.idiomatic: On his return he was made chief adjutant of the Dragon Swift Guard.

sentences.zh: 嘗盜官馬，貿直盡償博進，事發，獄具，有司引見講武殿，紹斌稱死罪。

translations.literal: He once stole government horses and used the proceeds entirely to pay gambling debts. When the affair came to light the case was complete; the authorities brought him before the Hall of Martial Instruction, and Shaobin declared himself guilty of a capital offense.
translations.idiomatic: He once stole government horses and spent the entire proceeds paying off gambling debts. When the crime was exposed and the case closed, officials brought him before the Hall of Martial Instruction, where Shaobin pleaded guilty to a capital crime.

sentences.zh: 太祖知其驍勇，欲宥之，執於門外，遣內侍私謂之曰：「爾今死有餘責。」

translations.literal: Taizu knew his valor and wished to pardon him. He had him held outside the gate and sent a palace attendant to tell him privately, "You now deserve death and more."
translations.idiomatic: Taizu knew how fierce a fighter he was and wished to spare him. He had Shaobin held outside the gate while a palace attendant told him privately, "By rights you deserve to die."

sentences.zh: 紹斌曰：「若恩貸臣死，當盡節以報。」

translations.literal: Shaobin said, "If Your Majesty in grace spares this servant's life, I shall devote my utmost loyalty in repayment."
translations.idiomatic: Shaobin replied, "If Your Majesty grants me my life, I will repay the favor with my utmost loyalty."

sentences.zh: 俄復引見，釋之，且密賜白金。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward he was summoned again, released, and secretly given white gold.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon summoned again, released, and secretly given silver as a personal gift.

sentences.zh: 會征江南，擇諸軍借事得五百人，為步鬬軍，令紹斌領之，及率雲騎二千，抵昇州城下，克獲居多。

translations.literal: When the Jiangnan campaign was undertaken, five hundred men were selected from various armies on loan for service and formed into a foot-combat army, which Shaobin was ordered to lead; he also led two thousand Cloud Cavalry and reached beneath the walls of Shengzhou, where his captures were the greater part.
translations.idiomatic: During the Jiangnan campaign, five hundred men were drafted on loan from various units to form a foot-combat detachment under Shaobin's command. He also led two thousand Cloud Cavalry to the walls of Shengzhou and accounted for the lion's share of enemy captures.

sentences.zh: 太祖親討河東，命紹斌從何繼筠扼契丹兵於北百井，奪賊皷幟而還。

translations.literal: Taizu personally campaigned against Hedong and ordered Shaobin to follow He Jijun in blocking Khitan troops at Beibaijing, seizing the enemy drums and banners and returning.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizu led a personal campaign against Hedong, he ordered Shaobin to join He Jijun in holding the Khitan at Beibaijing, where they seized enemy drums and banners and withdrew in triumph.

sentences.zh: 太平興國初，擢龍衛軍指揮使、領江州刺史。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Taiping Xingguo he was promoted to commander of the Longwei Army and concurrently prefect of Jiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Taiping Xingguo era (976–984) he was promoted to commander of the Dragon Guard Army and made prefect of Jiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 二年，梅山洞蠻叛，命與翟守素分往擊之。

translations.literal: In the second year the Meishan cave barbarians rebelled; he was ordered to strike them separately with Zhai Shousu.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year (977) the Meishan cave tribes rebelled; he and Zhai Shousu were sent to attack them on separate routes.

sentences.zh: 至邵州，聞蠻酋符漢陽死，去其居十里，大潰其眾，擒蠻二萬，令軍中取利劍二百斬之，餘五千遣歸諭諸洞，自是其黨帖服。

translations.literal: When he reached Shaozhou he heard that the barbarian chieftain Fu Hanyang was dead. Ten li from their settlement he routed their forces in great defeat, captured twenty thousand barbarians, ordered the army to take two hundred sharp swords and behead that many, sent the remaining five thousand back to instruct the various caves, and from then on their faction submitted.
translations.idiomatic: Reaching Shaozhou, he learned that the tribal chieftain Fu Hanyang was dead. Ten li from the enemy camp he routed their main force, took twenty thousand captives, had two hundred of them beheaded with sharp swords drawn from the ranks, and sent five thousand survivors home to warn the other cave settlements; thereafter the tribes submitted.

sentences.zh: 太宗賜以金帛、緡錢、金帶、鞍馬。

translations.literal: Taizong rewarded him with gold and silk, cash strings, a gold belt, and saddle horses.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong rewarded him with gold, silk, cash, a gold belt, and saddle horses.

sentences.zh: 歷天武、日騎軍指揮使，改馬步都軍頭，出戍鎮、定、高陽關。

translations.literal: He successively served as commander of the Tianwu and Riji [Daily Cavalry] armies, was changed to commander-in-chief of horse and foot, and went out to garrison Zhen, Ding, and Gaoyang Pass.
translations.idiomatic: He served in turn as commander of the Heavenly Martial and Daily Cavalry guards, was made commander-in-chief of horse and foot, and was posted to garrison Zhenzhou, Dingzhou, and Gaoyang Pass.

sentences.zh: 曹彬之攻幽州也，命為先鋒指揮使，數遇契丹兵鬥，奪牛羊、器甲。

translations.literal: When Cao Bin attacked Youzhou, he was ordered to serve as Vanguard Commandant; several times he met Khitan troops in battle and seized cattle, sheep, equipment, and armor.
translations.idiomatic: When Cao Bin attacked Youzhou, he was appointed Vanguard Commandant. He fought Khitan troops several times and seized cattle, sheep, equipment, and armor.

sentences.zh: 師還，召見便殿，加領溪州團練使，復遣屯北面。

translations.literal: When the army returned, he was summoned for audience in a side hall, additionally given command as Military Training Commissioner of Xizhou, and again sent to garrison the northern front.
translations.idiomatic: When the army returned, he was summoned to audience in a side hall, additionally made Military Training Commissioner of Xizhou, and again sent to garrison the northern front.

sentences.zh: 端拱元年，拜冀州防禦使，尋改解州。

translations.literal: In Duangong 1, he was appointed Defense Commissioner of Jizhou, and soon transferred to Jiezhou.
translations.idiomatic: In Duangong 1, he was appointed Defense Commissioner of Jizhou and soon transferred to Jiezhou.

sentences.zh: 淳化中，為河中、同、丹、坊、鄜、延、橫嶺蕃界都巡檢使。

translations.literal: During Chunhua he was made overall frontier inspector of the fan boundaries of Hezhong, Tong, Dan, Fang, Fu, Yan, and Hengling.
translations.idiomatic: During the Chunhua era (990–994) he was appointed overall frontier inspector along the tribal borders of Hezhong, Tongzhou, Danzhou, Fangzhou, Fuzhou, Yan'an, and Hengling.

sentences.zh: 會鄭文寶議城席雞城砦為清遠軍，紹斌與文寶領其役。

translations.literal: When Zheng Wenbao proposed fortifying the Xijicheng stockade as Qingyuan Army, Shaobin and Wenbao directed the work.
translations.idiomatic: When Zheng Wenbao proposed building up the Xijicheng stockade as Qingyuan Army, Shaobin and Wenbao jointly supervised the construction.

sentences.zh: 城畢，以文寶之請，命為知軍事。

translations.literal: When the fortification was completed, at Wenbao's request he was appointed to manage military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When the fort was finished, at Wenbao's request he was put in charge of its military affairs.

sentences.zh: 至道元年，拜會州觀察使，仍判解州，俄充靈州馬步軍部署。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhidao he was appointed observation commissioner of Huizhou and still concurrently administered Jiezhou; shortly afterward he was made deployer of the horse and foot armies of Lingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Zhidao (995) he was made observation commissioner of Huizhou while continuing to administer Jiezhou; soon after he was appointed overall deployer of the horse and foot forces at Lingzhou.

sentences.zh: 領徒入蕃討賊，斬首二千級，獲羊、馬、橐駝二萬計，馬以給諸軍之闕者。

translations.literal: He led his troops into the fan lands to punish bandits, beheaded two thousand, and captured on the order of twenty thousand sheep, horses, and camels; the horses were used to supply those lacking in the various armies.
translations.idiomatic: He led his men into the frontier to suppress raiders, took two thousand heads, and seized some twenty thousand sheep, horses, and camels, distributing the horses to units that were short of mounts.

sentences.zh: 捷聞，手詔嘉諭之。

translations.literal: When news of the victory arrived, an imperial autograph edict praised and instructed him.
translations.idiomatic: When word of the victory reached court, the emperor sent him a personal edict of commendation.

sentences.zh: 數部金粟帛詣靈武、清遠，遠人讋服不擾。

translations.literal: Several times he escorted gold, grain, and silk to Lingwu and Qingyuan; the distant peoples were awed into submission and did not disturb.
translations.idiomatic: He escorted supplies of gold, grain, and silk to Lingwu and Qingyuan on several occasions, and the frontier peoples, awed into submission, ceased their raids.

sentences.zh: 未幾，皇甫繼明、白守榮等督轉餉於靈州，紹斌率兵援接，抵鹹井。

translations.literal: Before long Huangfu Jiming, Bai Shourong, and others supervised the transport of provisions to Lingzhou; Shaobin led troops to reinforce and escort them, reaching Xianjing.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Huangfu Jiming, Bai Shourong, and others were supervising grain shipments to Lingzhou; Shaobin led troops to reinforce the convoy and reached Xianjing.

sentences.zh: 賊逾三千餘來薄陣，且行且鬥，至耀德，凡殺千人。

translations.literal: Bandits in excess of three thousand pressed the formation; fighting as they marched, they reached Yaode and in all killed a thousand men.
translations.idiomatic: More than three thousand enemy fighters pressed the column; fighting as they marched, they reached Yaode and killed a thousand of the enemy in all.

sentences.zh: 寇復尾後，紹斌為方陣，使被傷者居中，自將騎三百、步弩三百，與敵兵确於浦洛河，大敗之。

translations.literal: The raiders again followed from behind. Shaobin formed a square array, placed the wounded in the center, and personally led three hundred cavalry and three hundred foot crossbowmen to grapple with the enemy at the Puluo River and inflicted a great defeat.
translations.idiomatic: The raiders closed in again from the rear. Shaobin formed a square formation with the wounded in the center, then personally led three hundred horsemen and three hundred crossbowmen to engage the enemy at the Puluo River and routed them decisively.

sentences.zh: 初，守榮與紹斌為期，既而繼明卒，故後一日，遂為賊所圍。

translations.literal: Earlier Shourong and Shaobin had set a rendezvous; then Jiming died, so they were a day late and were surrounded by bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Shourong and Shaobin had agreed to rendezvous, but Jiming died en route, so they arrived a day late and found themselves surrounded.

sentences.zh: 守榮等欲擊之，紹斌曰：「蕃戎輕佻，勿棄輜重與戰，當按轡結陣徐行。」

translations.literal: Shourong and the others wished to attack them. Shaobin said, "The fan and Rong peoples are flighty; do not abandon the baggage train to give battle—hold the reins, form ranks, and advance slowly."
translations.idiomatic: Shourong and the others wanted to attack. Shaobin said, "These frontier warriors are rash; do not abandon the baggage train to fight. Hold formation and advance at a steady pace."

sentences.zh: 守榮等忿曰：「若但率兵來迎，勿預吾事。」

translations.literal: Shourong and the others said angrily, "If you would only lead troops to meet us, do not interfere in our affairs."
translations.idiomatic: Shourong and his men snapped, "If you mean to help, bring your troops to meet us—stay out of our business."

sentences.zh: 紹斌因率所部去輜重四五里。

translations.literal: Shaobin thereupon led his command four or five li away from the baggage train.
translations.idiomatic: Shaobin accordingly led his unit four or five li away from the baggage train.

sentences.zh: 繼遷初見紹斌旌旗，不敢擊。

translations.literal: When Jiqian first saw Shaobin's banners and flags, he did not dare attack.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Jiqian first sighted Shaobin's banners, he did not dare attack.

sentences.zh: 守榮等自欲邀功，與戰。

translations.literal: Shourong and the others themselves wished to claim merit and gave battle.
translations.idiomatic: Shourong and his men, eager for glory on their own account, gave battle.

sentences.zh: 賊先伏兵，以羸騎挑戰，已而伏發，守榮等戰敗，丁夫愕眙遁，蹂踐至死者眾。

translations.literal: The bandits had first laid ambush troops; with weak cavalry they provoked battle, then the ambush burst forth. Shourong and the others were defeated; the laborers stared in shock and fled, and many were trampled to death.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy had set an ambush first, baiting them with a few weak horsemen before springing the trap. Shourong's force was routed; laborers panicked and fled, and many were trampled to death in the stampede.

sentences.zh: 紹斌率所部徐還，一無遺失。

translations.literal: Shaobin led his command back slowly, without a single loss.
translations.idiomatic: Shaobin withdrew his unit at an orderly pace without losing a single man or pack animal.

sentences.zh: 至清遠，與張延州會食。

translations.literal: When he reached Qingyuan he joined Zhang Yanzhou for a meal.
translations.idiomatic: At Qingyuan he sat down to a meal with Zhang Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 見濠中人裸而呼曰：「我白守榮也。」

translations.literal: He saw a man in the moat, naked, calling out, "I am Bai Shourong."
translations.idiomatic: He saw a naked man in the moat shouting, "I am Bai Shourong!"

sentences.zh: 繩引而上，解衣遺之，遣內侍馬從順驛聞。

translations.literal: They hauled him up with a rope, gave him clothes from their own, and sent the palace attendant Ma Congshun by relay to report.
translations.idiomatic: They hauled him up on a rope, gave him their own clothes, and sent the palace attendant Ma Congshun by fast courier to report to court.

sentences.zh: 太宗益嘉之，優詔褒美。

translations.literal: Taizong praised him all the more and issued a gracious edict commending him.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong was all the more pleased and issued a gracious edict praising his conduct.

sentences.zh: 時命李繼隆、范廷召討繼遷，就命紹斌為本州都部署兼內外都巡檢使。

translations.literal: At the time Li Jilong and Fan Tingzhao were ordered to campaign against Jiqian; Shaobin was concurrently appointed overall deployer of the prefecture and overall internal and external inspector.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Jilong and Fan Tingzhao were ordered to campaign against Li Jiqian, Shaobin was concurrently made overall deployer of the prefecture and chief frontier inspector within and without.

sentences.zh: 繼隆以浦洛之敗上聞，言紹斌握兵不顧，自言「靈武非我不能守」，欲圖方面，有異志。

translations.literal: Jilong reported the Puluo defeat to the throne, saying Shaobin held his troops and would not heed others, declaring himself that "Lingwu cannot be held without me," wishing to secure a regional command, and harboring disloyal intent.
translations.idiomatic: Jilong reported the Puluo River disaster to court, accusing Shaobin of hoarding his troops and refusing to cooperate, boasting that "Lingwu cannot be held without me," and scheming for an independent regional command out of disloyal ambition.

sentences.zh: 太宗怒曰：「此昔嘗背太原來投，今又首鼠兩端，真賊臣也。」

translations.literal: Taizong said in anger, "This man once betrayed Taiyuan to come over to us; now he wavers between two sides again—truly a traitorous minister."
translations.idiomatic: Taizong said angrily, "He once betrayed Taiyuan to defect to us; now he wavers between two sides again—a traitor in truth."

sentences.zh: 即遣使捕繫詔獄鞫問，貶右監門衛率府副率、虢州安置。

translations.literal: He immediately sent envoys to seize and bind him, imprison him in the edict prison for interrogation, and demote him to deputy commandant of the Right Gate Guard command, with residence assigned at Guozhou.
translations.idiomatic: He immediately sent agents to arrest him, had him interrogated in the imperial prison, and demoted him to deputy commandant of the Right Gate Guard, with residence assigned at Guozhou.

sentences.zh: 真宗即位，召還，授右監門衛大將軍、領敘州刺史，尋改萊州防禦使，詔還其所籍居第，賜良馬十匹。

translations.literal: When Emperor Zhenzong took the throne, Shaobin was recalled and appointed great general of the Right Gate Guard Army and concurrently prefect of Xuzhou; soon he was changed to defense commissioner of Laizhou, and an edict restored his registered residence and bestowed ten fine horses.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhenzong succeeded to the throne, Shaobin was recalled and made great general of the Right Gate Guard while also serving as prefect of Xuzhou. He was soon transferred to defense commissioner of Laizhou, his registered residence was restored by edict, and he was granted ten fine horses.

sentences.zh: 調環、慶、靈州、清遠軍部署。

translations.literal: He was transferred to deployment commissioner over Huan, Qing, and Lingzhou and Qingyuan Army.
translations.idiomatic: He was reassigned as deployment commissioner over Huan, Qing, and Lingzhou and Qingyuan Army.

sentences.zh: 慶州有野雞族，數為寇掠，道路患之。

translations.literal: In Qingzhou there was the Yeji tribe, which repeatedly raided and plundered; travelers on the roads suffered from them.
translations.idiomatic: The Yeji tribe in Qing prefecture raided repeatedly and made the roads unsafe.

sentences.zh: 嘗有驍捷卒二十餘往邠州，為其掠奪，即馳告紹斌。

translations.literal: Once more than twenty valiant troops were going to Binzhou and were plundered by them; they immediately galloped to report to Shaobin.
translations.idiomatic: Once more than twenty elite troops bound for Binzhou were robbed by the tribe; they galloped at once to report to Shaobin.

sentences.zh: 紹斌召其酋帥三人，斷臂、馘、劓放還，寇感而化，帖服。

translations.literal: Shaobin summoned three of their chieftains, cut off their arms, took their ears, cut off their noses, and sent them back; the raiders were moved and reformed and submitted.
translations.idiomatic: Shaobin summoned three chieftains, had their arms severed, ears taken, and noses cut off, then sent them back. The raiders were awed into reform and submitted.

sentences.zh: 紹斌素勇悍，與同職頗不叶。

translations.literal: Shaobin had always been fierce and overbearing, and he rather failed to get along with colleagues of equal rank.
translations.idiomatic: Shaobin had long been fierce and overbearing and got on poorly with peers of equal rank.

sentences.zh: 轉運使宋太初每按部靈州、清遠，多貿市，紹斌語發其私，太初心銜之，及還朝，言紹斌之過，尋赴召，直其事。

translations.literal: Transport commissioner Song Taichu, whenever he inspected Lingzhou and Qingyuan, engaged in much trading; Shaobin spoke and exposed his private dealings. Taichu bore a grudge in his heart, and when he returned to court he reported Shaobin's faults. Soon Shaobin was summoned to audience and the matter was cleared.
translations.idiomatic: Transport commissioner Song Taichu traded heavily whenever he inspected Lingzhou and Qingyuan. Shaobin exposed his private dealings, and Taichu nursed a grudge. Back at court he denounced Shaobin, but when Shaobin was soon summoned to audience the charges were disproved.

sentences.zh: 咸平二年，北面寇警，復命為鎮、定、高陽關路押先鋒，隸傅潛。

translations.literal: In the second year of Xianping, when the northern frontier was alarmed by invasion, he was again appointed vanguard commander of the Zhen, Ding, and Gaoyang Pass circuit, subordinate to Fu Qian.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Xianping (999), with the northern frontier under threat, he was reappointed vanguard commander on the Zhen-Ding-Gaoyang Pass circuit under Fu Qian.

sentences.zh: 潛遣與石普並戍保州，普陰與知州楊嗣議出兵擊討之。

translations.literal: Qian sent him with Shi Pu to garrison Baozhou jointly; Pu secretly discussed with the prefect Yang Si sending troops out to strike and punish the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Qian posted him at Baozhou alongside Shi Pu; Pu secretly plotted with the prefect Yang Si to lead troops out against the enemy.

sentences.zh: 及夜，普、嗣未還，紹斌疑其敗衄，即領兵援之。

translations.literal: When night came and Pu and Si had not returned, Shaobin suspected they had been defeated and immediately led troops to reinforce them.
translations.idiomatic: When night fell and Pu and Si had still not returned, Shaobin feared they had been beaten and marched out to reinforce them at once.

sentences.zh: 普、嗣果為賊所困，度嚴涼河，頗喪師眾。

translations.literal: Pu and Si were indeed trapped by bandits; crossing the Yanliang River they lost a considerable part of their force.
translations.idiomatic: Pu and Si had indeed been trapped by the enemy; crossing the Yanliang River they suffered heavy losses.

sentences.zh: 及紹斌至，即合兵疾戰，獲一百四十餘人，以勞遷邢州觀察使。

translations.literal: When Shaobin arrived they united their forces and fought swiftly, capturing more than a hundred forty men; for his exertions he was transferred to observation commissioner of Xingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Shaobin arrived they joined forces and fought hard, taking more than a hundred forty prisoners; for his efforts he was promoted to observation commissioner of Xingzhou.

sentences.zh: 潛屯中山，紹斌三馳書於潛，且言：「邊眾大至，但列兵唐河南，背城與戰，慎無窮追。」

translations.literal: Qian was encamped at Zhongshan; Shaobin thrice sent urgent letters to Qian, also saying, "The frontier enemy has come in great numbers; only array troops south of the Tang River, fight with the city at your back, and beware of pursuing too far."
translations.idiomatic: Fu Qian held Zhongshan while Shaobin sent him three urgent dispatches warning, "The enemy has arrived in force. Deploy south of the Tang River and fight with the city at your back—do not pursue too far."

sentences.zh: 潛性巽懦，聞之益不敢出，賊眾益熾，焚劫城砦。

translations.literal: Qian was by nature compliant and timid; on hearing this he was all the more afraid to go out, the bandit forces grew ever fiercer, and they burned and plundered walled towns and stockades.
translations.idiomatic: Timid by nature, Fu Qian was even less willing to march out after hearing this; the enemy grew bolder and burned and looted towns and stockades.

sentences.zh: 車駕駐大名，召潛屬吏，詞逮紹斌，即遣使械繫，下御史臺鞫問，免官，黜為左衛率府副率，送往上都，禁其出入。

translations.literal: The imperial carriage was stationed at Daming; Qian's subordinate officials were summoned, and their testimony implicated Shaobin. Envoys were immediately sent to seize him in fetters, hand him to the Censorate for interrogation, strip his office, demote him to deputy commandant of the Left Guard command, send him to the upper capital, and forbid his coming and going.
translations.idiomatic: With the emperor at Daming, Fu Qian's staff were questioned and their testimony implicated Shaobin. Agents were sent at once to arrest him in chains; the Censorate tried him, stripped his rank, demoted him to deputy commandant of the Left Guard, sent him to the capital, and confined him to quarters.

sentences.zh: 五年，授右千牛衛將軍致仕。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he was appointed general of the Right Imperial Stables Guard and retired.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year (1002) he was granted retirement as general of the Right Imperial Stables Guard.

sentences.zh: 景德初，起為左龍武軍將軍、永城兵馬都監。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jingde he was recalled to serve as general of the Left Dragon Martial Army and overall supervisor of Yongcheng's troops and horses.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Jingde era (1004) he was recalled as general of the Left Dragon Martial Guard and overall military supervisor of Yongcheng.

sentences.zh: 三年，遷左監門衛大將軍。

translations.literal: In the third year he was transferred to senior general of the Left Gate Guard.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year (1006) he was promoted to senior general of the Left Gate Guard.

sentences.zh: 帝以紹斌久失職，不宜在衝要，乃徙考城都監。

translations.literal: The emperor considered that Shaobin had long been out of office and was unsuited to a critical post, so he was moved to overall supervisor of Kaocheng.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor judged that Shaobin, long out of favor, should not hold a critical post and transferred him to overall supervisor of Kaocheng.

sentences.zh: 大中祥符初，領長州刺史。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Dazhong Xiangfu he concurrently held the prefecture of Changzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Dazhong Xiangfu era (1008) he was made prefect of Changzhou.

sentences.zh: 從東封，朝覲壇就班，軍士建充庭旗，旗倒，壓紹斌仆地，遽起無傷。

translations.literal: He followed the eastern feng sacrifice; at the Hall of Imperial Audience he took his place in formation. Soldiers raised the court-canopy flags; a flag fell, knocked Shaobin to the ground, and he sprang up at once unharmed.
translations.idiomatic: He took part in the eastern feng sacrifice; as the court formed ranks at the Hall of Imperial Audience, soldiers raised the ceremonial canopy flags. One flag toppled and knocked Shaobin down, but he sprang up unhurt.

sentences.zh: 時紹斌已老，其壯健若此。

translations.literal: At the time Shaobin was already old, yet his vigor was such as this.
translations.idiomatic: By then Shaobin was already elderly, yet he remained as vigorous as this.

sentences.zh: 遷左領軍衛大將軍、領康州團練使、鞏縣都監。

translations.literal: He was transferred to senior general of the Left Leading Army Guard, concurrently regimental commissioner of Kangzhou, and overall supervisor of Gong County.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to senior general of the Left Leading Army Guard, made regimental commissioner of Kangzhou, and overall supervisor of Gong County.

sentences.zh: 二年，卒，年七十七。

translations.literal: In the second year he died, aged seventy-seven.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year (1009) he died at the age of seventy-seven.

sentences.zh: 紹斌長兵間，習戰法，其後累以格鬥立功，然性暴戾，故屢被黜。

translations.literal: Shaobin grew up amid warfare and was versed in tactics of battle; afterward he repeatedly won merit through hand-to-hand fighting, yet his nature was violent and overbearing, and for this reason he was often demoted.
translations.idiomatic: Shaobin had grown up in the army and mastered tactics; he won repeated distinction in combat, but his violent temper earned him repeated demotions.

sentences.zh: 子守信，為內殿崇班、閣門祗候。

translations.literal: His son Shouxin served as an inner-hall honored attendant and gatehouse usher of the Inner Palace Gate.
translations.idiomatic: His son Shouxin served as an inner-hall honored attendant and usher of the Inner Palace Gate.

sentences.zh: 王榮，定州人。

translations.literal: Wang Rong was a native of Dingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Rong was from Dingzhou.

sentences.zh: 父洪嗣，仕晉為本州十縣遊奕使。

translations.literal: His father Hongsi served Jin as patrol commissioner of the ten counties of the prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: His father Hongsi had served the Later Jin as patrol commissioner for the prefecture's ten counties.

sentences.zh: 榮少有膂力，事瀛州馬仁瑀為廝役。

translations.literal: Rong in youth had bodily strength and served Ma Renyu of Yingzhou as a menial.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth Rong was powerfully built and served Ma Renyu of Ying prefecture as a household servant.

sentences.zh: 太宗在藩邸，得隸左右。

translations.literal: When Taizong was in the princely residence, Rong came to serve at his left and right.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizong still held his princely residence, Rong entered his personal service.

sentences.zh: 即位，補殿前指揮使，稍遷本班都知、員僚直都虞候。

translations.literal: When Taizong took the throne, Rong was appointed commander of the Palace Front Guard; he was gradually promoted to chief adjutant of his unit and chief adjutant of the Direct Imperial Attendants.
translations.idiomatic: At Taizong's accession he was appointed a Palace Front Guard commander and gradually rose to chief adjutant of his unit and of the Direct Imperial Attendants.

sentences.zh: 盜發棣州，州兵不能捕，榮往討擒之。

translations.literal: When bandits rose in Dizhou and the prefectural troops could not capture them, Rong went to attack and seized them.
translations.idiomatic: When bandits broke out in Di prefecture and local troops could not catch them, Rong went out, defeated them, and took them captive.

sentences.zh: 加御前忠佐馬步軍都軍頭、領懿州刺史。

translations.literal: He was advanced to commander-in-chief of the Imperial Front Loyal Companion horse-and-foot army and concurrently prefect of Yizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to commander-in-chief of the emperor's loyal horse and foot auxiliaries and made prefect of Yizhou.

sentences.zh: 坐受秦王廷美宴勞，出為濮州馬軍教練使。

translations.literal: Because he accepted a feast and reward from Prince Qin Tingmei, he was sent out as horse-army training commissioner of Puzhou.
translations.idiomatic: For accepting entertainment from Prince Qin Tingmei, he was demoted to horse-army training commissioner of Pu prefecture.

sentences.zh: 未行，馬仁瑀子告榮與秦王親吏善，因狂言「我不久當得節帥」，坐削籍，流海島。

translations.literal: Before he departed, Ma Renyu's son reported that Rong was on good terms with Prince Qin's intimate clerks and, in wild talk, said, "Before long I shall obtain a commander's tally"; for the offense his name was struck from the rolls and he was banished to a sea island.
translations.idiomatic: Before he could leave, Ma Renyu's son reported that Rong was close to Prince Qin's personal staff and had boasted, "Before long I shall hold a regional command." He was stricken from the rolls and exiled to a sea island.

sentences.zh: 雍熙中召還，為副軍頭。

translations.literal: During Yongxi he was recalled and made deputy army commander.
translations.idiomatic: During the Yongxi era (984–987) he was recalled to court and made deputy army commander.

sentences.zh: 端拱初，改員寮左右直都虞候兼都軍頭，復領懿州刺史。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Duangong he was changed to chief adjutant of the Left and Right Direct Imperial Attendants and concurrently army commander-in-chief, and again held the prefecture of Yizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Duangong era (988) he was made chief adjutant of the Left and Right Direct Imperial Attendants and army commander-in-chief, and again served as prefect of Yizhou.

sentences.zh: 累遷龍衛都指揮使、領羅州團練使。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to overall commander of the Longwei Guard and concurrently regimental commissioner of Luozhou.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through successive promotions to overall commander of the Dragon Guard and regimental commissioner of Luozhou.

sentences.zh: 率兵戍遂城，邊騎來寇，擊敗之，擒千餘人。

translations.literal: He led troops to garrison Suicheng; frontier horsemen came to raid and he defeated them, capturing more than a thousand men.
translations.idiomatic: Leading troops to garrison Suicheng, he repelled a frontier cavalry raid and took more than a thousand prisoners.

sentences.zh: 召拜侍衛馬軍都虞候、峰州觀察使，出為定州行營都部署。

translations.literal: He was summoned and appointed chief adjutant of the Palace Horse Army and observation commissioner of Fengzhou, then sent out as overall deployer of the Dingzhou field headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned to court as chief adjutant of the Palace Cavalry and observation commissioner of Fengzhou, then dispatched as overall deployer of the Dingzhou field headquarters.

sentences.zh: 榮粗率，所為不中理，侵取官地蒔蔬，吝惜公錢，不以勞將士，且母老不迎養，供給甚薄。

translations.literal: Rong was coarse and rash; his conduct was unreasonable. He seized government land to plant vegetables, was stingy with public funds and did not reward the officers and soldiers for their labors, and though his mother was old he did not bring her to live with him and provided for her very meagerly.
translations.idiomatic: Rong was coarse and impulsive, and his conduct was improper: he seized government land for vegetable plots, hoarded public funds and failed to reward his troops, and though his mother was elderly he neither brought her to live with him nor provided adequately for her upkeep.

sentences.zh: 太宗聞而怒曰：「忠臣出於孝子之門，榮事親若此，竄逐之餘，凶行弗悛，豈可復置左右，效晉帝養成張彥澤邪？」

translations.literal: Taizong heard of it and said in anger, "Loyal ministers come from the households of filial sons. Rong serves his parents like this; after banishment and exile his vicious conduct has not changed—how can he again be placed at one's side, as the Jin emperor nurtured Zhang Yanzhe?"
translations.idiomatic: When Taizong heard of it he said angrily, "Loyal ministers come from filial households. Rong treats his parents like this; even after exile his vicious ways have not changed—how can we keep him at court, as the Later Jin emperor nurtured Zhang Yanzhe?"

sentences.zh: 即詔罷，督責，授右驍衛大將軍。

translations.literal: He immediately issued an edict removing him from office, censured him, and appointed him senior general of the Right Valiant Cavalry Guard.
translations.idiomatic: He immediately ordered Rong dismissed, rebuked him sharply, and appointed him senior general of the Right Valiant Cavalry Guard.

sentences.zh: 寄班供奉官張明護定州兵，睹榮不法，間嘗規正。

translations.literal: The probationary attendant Zhang Ming guarded the Dingzhou troops, witnessed Rong's unlawful acts, and from time to time tried to correct him.
translations.idiomatic: The probationary palace attendant Zhang Ming was assigned to oversee Dingzhou troops; seeing Rong's misconduct, he occasionally tried to correct him.

sentences.zh: 榮護短，每疾其攻己。

translations.literal: Rong shielded his faults and always resented Ming's attacks on him.
translations.idiomatic: Rong was touchy about his faults and resented every criticism Ming aimed at him.

sentences.zh: 莊宅使王斌亦監軍是州，素與榮善，意明構榮之罪，因摭明以報怨。

translations.literal: The Estates Commissioner Wang Bin also supervised the army in that prefecture and was on good terms with Rong; he supposed Ming was fabricating charges against Rong and seized on Ming to repay a grudge.
translations.idiomatic: Estates Commissioner Wang Bin, who also supervised troops in that prefecture and was on friendly terms with Rong, assumed Ming was fabricating charges and seized on Ming's conduct to settle a grudge.

sentences.zh: 下樞密院問狀，皆不實。

translations.literal: The case was sent down to the Bureau of Military Affairs for investigation; none of the charges proved true.
translations.idiomatic: The Bureau of Military Affairs investigated the charges and found none of them substantiated.

sentences.zh: 上怒，語左右曰：「張明起賤微中，以蹴鞠事朕，潔己小心，見於輩流。

translations.literal: The emperor was angry and said to those beside him, "Zhang Ming rose from humble origins, served me through cuju, kept himself clean and cautious, and stood out among his peers.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was angry and told his attendants, "Zhang Ming rose from humble origins, served me through cuju football, and has always conducted himself with scrupulous care—he stands out among his peers.

sentences.zh: 夫刑罰之加，必當其罪。

translations.literal: When punishment is applied, it must match the crime.
translations.idiomatic: Punishment must fit the crime.

sentences.zh: 今王斌以榮故而曲奏明罪，欲致刑憲，苟失其當，適足以快榮之心，而誣罔得以肆行矣。

translations.literal: Now Wang Bin, for Rong's sake, has bent the facts to report Ming's crimes and wishes to bring him under penal law. If the measure is wrong, it would only gratify Rong's heart, and calumny would be allowed to run riot.
translations.idiomatic: Now Wang Bin, for Rong's sake, has distorted the facts to prosecute Ming. If punishment misses its mark, it will only gratify Rong while letting slander run unchecked.

sentences.zh: 且榮淩轢同類，事君與親鮮竭其力。

translations.literal: Moreover Rong bullies his peers, and in serving his ruler and his parents he rarely exhausts his strength.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover Rong bullies his peers and has scarcely given his full devotion either to the throne or to his parents.

sentences.zh: 國家賞罰之柄，非所敢私，將帥之職，非裨校同。

translations.literal: The state's power of reward and punishment is not something I dare treat privately; the office of commander is not the same as that of a junior officer.
translations.idiomatic: The power of reward and punishment belongs to the state, not to my private favor; a field commander's office is not the same as a junior officer's.

sentences.zh: 朕豈黨張明而棄王榮哉，奈何不求直於理之當也？」

translations.literal: How would I take Zhang Ming's side and abandon Wang Rong? Why not seek what is straight in what reason requires?"
translations.idiomatic: Am I to favor Zhang Ming and abandon Wang Rong? Why not simply seek what justice requires?"

sentences.zh: 遂賜勞明緡錢、束帛，榮遷右羽林軍大將軍。

translations.literal: He thereupon granted Ming a reward of cash strings and silks; Rong was transferred to senior general of the Right Forest Guard.
translations.idiomatic: He rewarded Ming with cash and silks and transferred Rong to senior general of the Right Forest Guard.

sentences.zh: 真宗即位，領獎州刺史，尋授濱州防禦使，遷涇原儀渭駐泊部署。

translations.literal: When Emperor Zhenzong took the throne, Rong concurrently held the prefecture of Jiangzhou; soon he was appointed defense commissioner of Binzhou and transferred to deployment commissioner of the Jingyuan, Yi, and Wei garrison.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhenzong succeeded to the throne, Rong was made prefect of Jiangzhou, soon appointed defense commissioner of Bin prefecture, and then transferred to command the Jingyuan-Yi-Wei garrison deployment.

sentences.zh: 咸平二年，車駕北征，召為貝、冀行營副都部署。

translations.literal: In the second year of Xianping, when the imperial carriage campaigned north, he was summoned to be deputy overall deployment commissioner of the Bei and Ji field headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Xianping (999), when the emperor marched north, Rong was summoned as deputy commander of the Bei-Ji field headquarters.

sentences.zh: 師旋，復還涇原。

translations.literal: When the army returned, he again went back to Jingyuan.
translations.idiomatic: When the campaign ended he returned to Jingyuan.

sentences.zh: 明年，援送靈武芻糧，疏於智略，不嚴斥候，至積石，夜為蕃寇所劫，營部大亂，眾亡殆盡。

translations.literal: The next year, while escorting fodder for Lingwu, he was deficient in strategy and did not strictly post scouts; at Jishi, by night he was raided by frontier bandits, the camp fell into great disorder, and his force was nearly wiped out.
translations.idiomatic: The next year, while convoying fodder to Lingwu, he showed poor judgment and failed to post adequate scouts. At Jishi his camp was ambushed at night by frontier raiders, his command collapsed in chaos, and nearly all his men were lost.

sentences.zh: 法當誅，恕死，除名配均州。

translations.literal: By law he deserved execution; his life was spared, his name was removed from the rolls, and he was assigned to Junzhou.
translations.idiomatic: By law he deserved death, but his life was spared; he was stricken from the rolls and exiled to Junzhou.

sentences.zh: 六年，起為左衛將軍。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he was raised up as general of the Left Guard.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year (1003) he was restored to office as a general of the Left Guard.

sentences.zh: 景德初，權判左金吾街仗司事。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jingde he was given provisional charge of the Left Golden Crow Street Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Jingde era he was given provisional charge of the Left Golden Crow Street Guard.

sentences.zh: 上觀兵澶淵，契丹遊騎涉河冰抵濮州境，命為黃河南岸都巡檢使，與鄭懷德自行在領龍衛兵追襲。

translations.literal: When the emperor reviewed troops at Chanyuan, Khitan scouting horsemen crossed the river ice and reached the borders of Puzhou; Rong was appointed overall inspector south of the Yellow River and, with Zheng Huaide from the imperial encampment, led Longwei troops in pursuit.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor inspected troops at Chanyuan, Khitan scouting parties crossed the frozen river into Puzhou territory; Rong was made overall inspector south of the Yellow River and, with Zheng Huaide from the imperial camp, led Dragon Guard troops in pursuit.

sentences.zh: 時已詔滄州部署荊嗣先率所部屯淄、青，遣榮等合兵邀擊之。

translations.literal: An edict had already ordered the Cangzhou deployer Jing Sixian to lead his command to encamp at Zi and Qing; Rong and others were sent to unite forces and intercept the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: An edict had already ordered the Cangzhou deployer Jing Sixian to encamp his forces in Zi and Qing prefectures; Rong and others were sent to join forces and intercept the enemy.

sentences.zh: 二年，遷左神武軍大將軍、領恩州刺史。

translations.literal: In the second year he was transferred to senior general of the Left Divine Martial Army and concurrently prefect of Enzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year (1005) he was promoted to senior general of the Left Divine Martial Guard and made prefect of Enzhou.

sentences.zh: 郊祀，改左龍武軍、領達州團練使。

translations.literal: At the suburban sacrifice he was changed to the Left Dragon Martial Army and concurrently regimental commissioner of Dazhou.
translations.idiomatic: After the suburban sacrifice he was transferred to the Left Dragon Martial Guard and made regimental commissioner of Dazhou.

sentences.zh: 大中祥符中，遷左衛大將軍、領昌州防禦使。

translations.literal: During Dazhong Xiangfu he was transferred to senior general of the Left Guard and concurrently defense commissioner of Changzhou.
translations.idiomatic: During the Dazhong Xiangfu era he was promoted to senior general of the Left Guard and made defense commissioner of Changzhou.

sentences.zh: 六年，朝太清宮，命為河南府駐泊都監。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he attended audience at the Grand Pure Palace and was appointed overall supervisor of the Henan prefectural garrison.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year (1013) he attended court at the Grand Pure Palace and was appointed overall supervisor of the Henan prefectural garrison.

sentences.zh: 九年，卒，年七十。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he died, aged seventy.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year (1016) he died at the age of seventy.

sentences.zh: 官其一子。

translations.literal: One of his sons was given an official post.
translations.idiomatic: One of his sons was granted an official appointment.

sentences.zh: 榮善射，嘗引強注屋棟，矢入木數寸，時人目為「王硬弓」。

translations.literal: Rong was skilled at archery; he once drew a powerful bow and shot at a roof beam, the arrow entering the wood several inches, and people of the time called him "Wang the Hard Bow."
translations.idiomatic: Rong was an expert archer; once he drew a heavy bow and shot at a roof beam, driving the arrow several inches into the wood, and contemporaries nicknamed him "Wang the Hard Bow."

sentences.zh: 楊瓊，汾州西河人。

translations.literal: Yang Qiong was a native of Xihe in Fenzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Qiong came from Xihe county in Fen prefecture.

sentences.zh: 幼事馮繼業，以材勇稱。

translations.literal: In youth he served Feng Jiye and was renowned for talent and courage.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth he served under Feng Jiye and won a reputation for ability and valor.

sentences.zh: 太宗召置帳下。

translations.literal: Emperor Taizong summoned him and placed him under his personal command.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Taizong summoned him to serve in his personal guard.

sentences.zh: 即位，隸御龍直，三遷神勇指揮使。

translations.literal: When [Taizong] took the throne, he was assigned to the Imperial Dragon Direct [Guard]; after three promotions he became commander of the Divine Valor command.
translations.idiomatic: After Taizong's accession he joined the Imperial Dragon Guard and rose through three ranks to commander of the Divine Valor corps.

sentences.zh: 從征太原，以勞補御龍直指揮使。

translations.literal: He followed the campaign against Taiyuan; for his labors he was appointed commander of the Imperial Dragon Direct [Guard].
translations.idiomatic: He marched on the Taiyuan campaign and, rewarded for his exertions, was made commander of the Imperial Dragon Guard.

sentences.zh: 雍熙初，改弩直都虞候兼御前忠佐馬步都軍頭、領顯州刺史。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yongxi, he was changed to chief adjutant of the Crossbow Direct [Guard], concurrently chief of the Imperial Front Loyal Companion horse-and-foot army, and he held concurrently the post of prefect of Xianzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Yongxi era (984) he became chief adjutant of the Crossbow Guard while also serving as commander-in-chief of the emperor's loyal horse and foot auxiliaries and acting prefect of Xianzhou.

sentences.zh: 淳化中，李順叛蜀，瓊往夔、峽擒賊招安，領兵自峽上，與賊遇，累戰抵渝、合，與尹元、裴莊分路進討，克資、普二州、雲安軍，斬首數千級。

translations.literal: In the Chunhua era, Li Shun rebelled in Shu; Qiong went to Kuizhou and the Gorges to capture rebels and win them over, led troops up from the gorges, met the rebels, fought repeatedly reaching Yu and He, and with Yin Yuan and Pei Zhuang advanced by separate routes to attack, capturing the two prefectures of Zi and Pu and the Yun'an Army commandery, beheading several thousand at the head-count.
translations.idiomatic: During the Chunhua era (990–994), when Li Shun rose in rebellion in Shu, Qiong was sent to Kuizhou and the Three Gorges to suppress the rebels and win defectors. He led his troops upstream from the gorges, clashed repeatedly with the enemy as far as Yu and He prefectures, and together with Yin Yuan and Pei Zhuang struck along separate routes, taking Zi and Pu prefectures and Yun'an military district and slaying several thousand foes.

sentences.zh: 詔書嘉獎，遣使即軍中真拜單州刺史。

translations.literal: An edict commended and rewarded him; an envoy was sent to the army to appoint him in full as prefect of Shanzhou on the spot.
translations.idiomatic: The court issued a commendatory edict and dispatched an envoy to the field to appoint him prefect of Shanzhou there and then.

sentences.zh: 至道初，召還共職。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhidao, he was recalled to resume his duties together [with the court].
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Zhidao era (995) he was recalled to resume his post at court.

sentences.zh: 明年，徙知霸州兼鈐轄。

translations.literal: The next year, he was transferred to administer Bazhou concurrently as military commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was transferred to govern Bazhou while also serving as its military commissioner.

sentences.zh: 未幾，改防禦使，靈慶路副都部署、河外都巡檢使。

translations.literal: Before long, he was changed to defense commissioner, deputy overall deployment commissioner of the Lingqing circuit, and overall frontier inspector beyond the river.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly afterward he was made defense commissioner, deputy commander of the Lingqing frontier circuit, and chief inspector of posts beyond the Yellow River.

sentences.zh: 賊累寇疆，瓊固捍有功。

translations.literal: The rebels repeatedly raided the borderlands; Qiong firmly defended and had merit.
translations.idiomatic: When enemy raids struck the frontier again and again, Qiong's stout defense earned him repeated credit.

sentences.zh: 導黃河，溉民田數千頃。

translations.literal: He channeled the Yellow River to irrigate several thousand qing of the people's fields.
translations.idiomatic: He diverted the Yellow River to irrigate several thousand acres of farmland.

sentences.zh: 敗賊於合河鎮北，擒獲人畜居多。

translations.literal: He defeated the rebels north of Hehe Town, capturing people and livestock in great numbers.
translations.idiomatic: North of Hehe Town he routed the enemy and took a great haul of captives and livestock.

sentences.zh: 賊騎五百掠城下，擊破之，追北三十里。

translations.literal: Five hundred rebel horsemen plundered below the city; he struck and broke them, pursuing north thirty li.
translations.idiomatic: When five hundred enemy horsemen raided beneath the walls, he shattered them and chased the fugitives thirty li northward.

sentences.zh: 並賜詔嘉諭。

translations.literal: In each case an edict was bestowed commending and instructing him.
translations.idiomatic: The throne rewarded each exploit with an edict of commendation.

sentences.zh: 咸平二年，命為涇原儀渭邠寧環慶清遠軍靈州路副都部署。

translations.literal: In the second year of Xianping, he was ordered to be deputy overall deployment commissioner of the Jingyuan, Yi, Wei, Bin, Ning, Huan, Qing, Qingyuan Army, and Lingzhou route.
translations.idiomatic: In 999 he was appointed deputy commander of the northwestern frontier stretching from Jingyuan through Yi, Wei, Bin, Ning, Huan, and Qing prefectures to Qingyuan garrison and Lingzhou.

sentences.zh: 尋徙鎮、定、高陽關三路押策先鋒，屯定州之北。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to be vanguard leader of the three routes of Zhen, Ding, and Gaoyang Pass, encamped north of Dingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon shifted to lead the vanguard of the Zhen, Ding, and Gaoyang Pass frontier commands, with his camp north of Dingzhou.

sentences.zh: 明年，副王超為鎮州都部署，再遷環慶，徙定州。

translations.literal: The next year, he served as deputy to Wang Chao as overall deployment commissioner of Zhenzhou; again he was transferred to Huanqing, then moved to Dingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he served under Wang Chao as deputy commander at Zhenzhou, then was posted to Huanqing and finally transferred to Dingzhou.

sentences.zh: 四年，召還，以鄜州觀察使充靈、環十州軍副都部署兼安撫副使。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, he was recalled; as observation commissioner of Fuzhou he filled the post of deputy overall deployment commissioner of the ten prefectures and armies of Ling and Huan, concurrently deputy pacification commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In 1001 he was recalled and made observation commissioner of Fuzhou while serving as deputy commander of the ten frontier prefectures around Ling and Huan and as deputy pacification commissioner.

sentences.zh: 嘗遣使諭旨，賊若寇清遠及青岡、白馬砦，即合兵與戰。

translations.literal: On one occasion an envoy was sent to convey the imperial intent: if the rebels raided Qingyuan and the stockades of Qinggang and White Horse, he was immediately to combine forces and give battle.
translations.idiomatic: The court had once sent word that if the enemy struck Qingyuan or the Qinggang and White Horse stockades, he was to unite his forces and give battle at once.

sentences.zh: 是秋，果長圍清遠，頓積石河。

translations.literal: That autumn, they indeed made a prolonged siege of Qingyuan, encamping at the Jishi River.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn the Tanguts duly laid prolonged siege to Qingyuan and pitched camp on the Jishi River.

sentences.zh: 清遠屢走間使詣瓊請濟師，瓊將悉出兵為援，鈐轄內園使馮守規、都監崇儀使張繼能曰：「敵近，重兵在前，繼無以進，不可悉往。」

translations.literal: Qingyuan repeatedly sent stealth messengers to Qiong requesting relief troops; Qiong was about to lead out the entire army as reinforcements, when military commissioner and Inner Park envoy Feng Shougui and supervisory commissioner and Honored Ritual envoy Zhang Jineng said: "The enemy is near; with the main force out front, those following will have no way to advance—they cannot all go."
translations.idiomatic: Qingyuan repeatedly slipped messengers through the lines begging Qiong for relief. He was preparing to march out with his whole army when Military Commissioner Feng Shougui of the Inner Park and Supervisory Commissioner Zhang Jineng objected: "The foe is too close—in sending the entire main body forward, nothing can follow behind. We cannot send everyone."

sentences.zh: 乃止命副部署海州團練使潘璘、都監西京左藏庫劉文質率兵六千赴之，且曰：「伺我之繼至。」

translations.literal: He therefore stopped and ordered deputy deployment commissioner and Haizhou training commissioner Pan Lin and supervisory commissioner and Left Storehouse of the Western Capital Liu Wenzhi to lead six thousand troops to go to their aid, saying moreover: "Wait for us to follow and arrive."
translations.idiomatic: So he held back and dispatched Deputy Commander Pan Lin of Haizhou and Supervisory Commissioner Liu Wenzhi of the Western Capital Left Storehouse with six thousand men, telling them, "Wait until we can come up behind you."

sentences.zh: 瓊逗遛不進，頓慶州。

translations.literal: Qiong delayed and did not advance, halting at Qingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Qiong himself dallied and never advanced, lingering at Qingzhou.

sentences.zh: 寇鼓兵攻南門，其子阿移攻北門，堙壕斷橋以戰。

translations.literal: The invaders beat drums and attacked the south gate; his son Ayi attacked the north gate; they filled moats and cut bridges to fight.
translations.idiomatic: The besiegers drummed up their assault on the south gate while the khan's son Ayi struck the north; they filled in the moat and broke the bridges to press the attack.

sentences.zh: 瓊遣鈐轄李讓督精卒六百往援，至則城陷矣。

translations.literal: Qiong sent military commissioner Li Rang to supervise six hundred picked troops to go reinforce; when they arrived, the city had already fallen.
translations.idiomatic: Qiong sent Military Commissioner Li Rang with six hundred elite troops to relieve the garrison, but they arrived only after the city had fallen.

sentences.zh: 賊泊青岡城下，瓊與守規、繼能方緩行出師，及聞清遠之敗，益恇怯不前。

translations.literal: The rebels moored at Qinggang below the city; Qiong with Shougui and Jineng had just been proceeding slowly in marching out, and when they heard of Qingyuan's defeat, they became all the more timid and fearful and did not advance.
translations.idiomatic: With the enemy anchored below Qinggang, Qiong, Shougui, and Jineng were only then setting out at an unhurried pace; once news of Qingyuan's fall reached them, they grew still more timid and hung back.

sentences.zh: 順州刺史王瑰普謂瓊曰：「青岡地遠水泉，非屯師計，願棄之。」

translations.literal: Shunzhou prefect Wang Guipu said to Qiong: "Qinggang's terrain is remote from water springs—not a plan for encamping troops; I wish to abandon it."
translations.idiomatic: Wang Guipu, prefect of Shunzhou, urged Qiong: "Qinggang lies too far from reliable water to hold troops—we should give it up."

sentences.zh: 瓊合謀焚芻糧兵仗，驅老幼以出。

translations.literal: Qiong joined in the plot, burned fodder, grain, and weapons, and drove out the old and young.
translations.idiomatic: Qiong agreed, burned stores of fodder, grain, and arms, and drove out the noncombatants.

sentences.zh: 瓊卻師，退保洪德砦，寇威浸熾，未嘗交一鋒。

translations.literal: Qiong withdrew the army, falling back to defend Hongde stockade; the invaders' menace gradually grew fierce, and he never once crossed blades with them.
translations.idiomatic: Qiong pulled his army back to Hongde stockade while the enemy's power swelled; he never once offered battle.

sentences.zh: 事聞於上，傳召瓊輩，悉繫御史獄，治罪當死。

translations.literal: When the matter reached the throne, [the court] urgently summoned Qiong and his companions; all were imprisoned in the Censorate jail, and under the law the penalty was death.
translations.idiomatic: When word reached the emperor, Qiong and his fellows were summoned back and clapped in the Censorate prison, where the statute called for death.

sentences.zh: 兵部尚書張齊賢等議請如律，詔特貸命，削官，長流崖州，繼能、守規輩同坐，籍其家業。

translations.literal: Minister of War Zhang Qixian and others deliberated and requested application of the statute; an edict specially pardoned their lives, stripped their ranks, and exiled them for life to Yazhou; Jineng, Shougui, and their ilk shared the sentence, and their family estates were confiscated.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of War Zhang Qixian and others urged applying the death penalty, but an edict specially spared their lives, stripped their offices, and banished them for life to Yazhou; Jineng, Shougui, and the rest shared the punishment, and their household property was forfeited to the state.

sentences.zh: 明年，移道州。

translations.literal: The next year, he was moved to Daozhou.
translations.idiomatic: The following year his place of exile was shifted to Daozhou.

sentences.zh: 景德初，起為右領軍衛將軍。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jingde, he was raised up as general of the Right Leading Army guard.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Jingde era (1004) he was restored to rank as a general of the Right Leading Army Guard.

sentences.zh: 分司西京。

translations.literal: He served in a nominal post at the Western Capital.
translations.idiomatic: He held an honorary post in the Western Capital.

sentences.zh: 累遷左領軍衛大將軍、領賀州團練使、知兗州。

translations.literal: After repeated promotions he became great general of the Left Leading Army guard, concurrently training commissioner of Hezhou, and administrator of Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through several promotions to great general of the Left Leading Army Guard, training commissioner of Hezhou, and prefect of Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 有州卒自言得神術，能飛行空中，州人頗惑。

translations.literal: A garrison soldier claimed he had attained divine arts and could fly through the air; the people of the prefecture were quite deluded.
translations.idiomatic: A soldier in his command claimed supernatural powers and the ability to fly through the air, and many in Yanzhou were taken in.

sentences.zh: 瓊捕至，折其足，奏戮之。

translations.literal: Qiong captured him, broke his legs, and memorialized to execute him.
translations.idiomatic: Qiong had him seized, broke both his legs, and memorialized the throne to put him to death.

sentences.zh: 五年，卒，年六十七。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, he died, aged sixty-seven.
translations.idiomatic: He died in 1008 at the age of sixty-seven.

sentences.zh: 錄其子舜臣為奉職。

translations.literal: His son Shunchen was entered on the register as a palace attendant.
translations.idiomatic: His son Shunchen was enrolled in palace service as an attendant.

sentences.zh: 長子舜賓，內殿崇班、閤門祗候。

translations.literal: His eldest son Shunbin was an Inner Hall honored cohort and Gate Chamberlain.
translations.idiomatic: His eldest son Shunbin held posts as an Inner Hall honored cohort and gate chamberlain.

sentences.zh: 錢守俊

translations.literal: Qian Shoujun
translations.idiomatic: Qian Shoujun

sentences.zh: 錢守俊，濮州雷澤人。

translations.literal: Qian Shoujun was a native of Leize in Puzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Qian Shoujun came from Leize in Pu prefecture.

sentences.zh: 少勇鷙，嘗為盜陂澤中，稱「轉陂鶻」。

translations.literal: In youth he was fierce and audacious; he once was a bandit among the marshes and lakes, styled "the Turning-Marsh Falcon."
translations.idiomatic: As a youth he was ferociously bold and had once robbed among the marshlands, where men called him "the Marsh-Hawk."

sentences.zh: 周顯德中，應募為鐵騎卒。

translations.literal: In the Xiande era of Zhou, he answered the recruitment as a soldier of the Iron Horse [Guard].
translations.idiomatic: During the Xiande era (954–959) he enlisted as a trooper in the Iron Horse Guard.

sentences.zh: 早事太祖，從征淮南，戰紫金山，下壽春，獲戰艦千餘艘。

translations.literal: Early he served the Taizu, followed the Huainan campaign, fought at Purple Gold Mountain, took Shouchun, and captured more than a thousand war vessels.
translations.idiomatic: He entered Taizu's service early, marched on Huainan, fought at Purple Gold Mountain, took Shouchun, and seized more than a thousand enemy warships.

sentences.zh: 繼從克關南。

translations.literal: He then followed in the capture of Guannan.
translations.idiomatic: He went on to take part in the recovery of Guannan.

sentences.zh: 宋初，補禁衛，隸散員直。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Song, he was appointed to the forbidden guard and was assigned to the Loose Retainer Direct [corps].
translations.idiomatic: At the founding of the dynasty he joined the palace guard and was posted to the Loose Retainer Direct corps.

sentences.zh: 乾德中，轉殿前班都知。

translations.literal: In the Qiande era, he was transferred to be commander of the Hall Front rank.
translations.idiomatic: During the Qiande era (963–968) he became commander of the Hall Front rank.

sentences.zh: 尋征太原，方戰，矢中左足，拔而復進，格鬥不已。

translations.literal: Soon he campaigned against Taiyuan; in the midst of battle an arrow struck his left foot; he pulled it out and advanced again, grappling without cease.
translations.idiomatic: He soon marched on Taiyuan; mid-battle an arrow pierced his left foot, but he pulled it out, pressed forward, and kept fighting without pause.

sentences.zh: 還，改東西班指揮使，遷馬步軍副都軍頭。

translations.literal: On return, he was changed to commander of the East-West Classes and promoted to deputy chief of the horse-and-foot army.
translations.idiomatic: After the campaign he was made commander of the East-West Classes and promoted to deputy chief of the army.

sentences.zh: 太平興國四年，命與張紹、李神祐、劉承珪率師屯定州，以備北邊。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Taiping Xingguo, he was ordered with Zhang Shao, Li Shenyou, and Liu Chenggui to lead troops encamped at Dingzhou to guard the northern frontier.
translations.idiomatic: In 979 he was ordered together with Zhang Shao, Li Shenyou, and Liu Chenggui to take troops to Dingzhou to guard the northern frontier.

sentences.zh: 俄加秩領演州刺史，移屯趙州。

translations.literal: Shortly he was given added rank and held concurrently the prefecture of Yanzhou, and his encampment was moved to Zhaozhou.
translations.idiomatic: He soon received added rank as acting prefect of Yan prefecture and shifted his camp to Zhaozhou.

sentences.zh: 又從征范陽，師還，道遇敵，戰於徐河，斬首千級，奪馬百匹。

translations.literal: He again followed the campaign against Fanyang; as the army returned, on the road they met the enemy and fought at the Xu River, beheading a thousand at the head-count and seizing a hundred horses.
translations.idiomatic: He joined the expedition against Fanyang and, on the march home, intercepted the enemy at the Xu River, killing a thousand men and capturing a hundred horses.

sentences.zh: 雍熙三年，命將北征，田重進出飛狐道，守俊以偏師為援，邊騎雲集，守俊按甲從容進戰，大敗之。

translations.literal: In the third year of Yongxi, he was ordered as general on the northern expedition; Tian Zhongjin went out by the Flying Fox route, Shoujun with a detached force served as reinforcement—the border horsemen gathered like clouds—Shoujun held his armor and advanced to battle at an easy pace, and utterly defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: In 986 he commanded on the northern expedition while Tian Zhongjin advanced through Flying Fox Pass; Shoujun led a supporting column. When enemy horsemen swarmed the frontier, he held his ranks, engaged at a deliberate pace, and inflicted a crushing defeat.

sentences.zh: 連護屯兵於趙、定。

translations.literal: In succession he protected and garrisoned troops at Zhao and Ding.
translations.idiomatic: He went on to garrison troops on the Zhao and Ding frontier.

sentences.zh: 代還，掌軍頭引見司。

translations.literal: When his tour ended and he returned, he took charge of the Army Chief Presentation Office.
translations.idiomatic: After his tour of duty he returned to head the Army Presentation Office.

sentences.zh: 淳化三年，出為單州團練使。

translations.literal: In the third year of Chunhua, he went out as training commissioner of Shanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In 992 he was posted out as training commissioner of Shanzhou.

sentences.zh: 又明年，改遷齊州。

translations.literal: Again the next year, he was changed and transferred to Qizhou.
translations.idiomatic: The year after he was transferred to Qizhou.

sentences.zh: 時河西蕃部內擾，命以副都部署鎮其地。

translations.literal: At the time the Hexi tribal factions were in internal disturbance; he was ordered as deputy overall deployment commissioner to garrison that region.
translations.idiomatic: When the Hexi tribes fell into civil strife, he was appointed deputy frontier commander to pacify the region.

sentences.zh: 既而徙屯石州，數改官。

translations.literal: Before long he was moved to garrison at Shizhou, and his office was changed several times.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon shifted to garrison Shizhou and underwent several further reassignments.

sentences.zh: 時有言守俊病且老，握重兵不堪其職。

translations.literal: At the time someone said Shoujun was ill and old, holding heavy military force but unfit for his post.
translations.idiomatic: Reports circulated that Shoujun was sick and aged and no longer fit to command a large army.

sentences.zh: 召還，授左領軍衛大將軍、領潘州防禦使、權金吾街仗。

translations.literal: He was recalled and appointed great general of the Left Leading Army guard, concurrently defense commissioner of Panzhou, and acting commander of the Jinwu street guard.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled and made great general of the Left Leading Army Guard, defense commissioner of Panzhou, and acting commander of the Jinwu street guard.

sentences.zh: 大中祥符三年卒，年八十一。

translations.literal: In the third year of Dazhong Xiangfu, he died, aged eighty-one.
translations.idiomatic: He died in 1010 at the age of eighty-one.

sentences.zh: 守俊累從軍征討，前後中三十六創。

translations.literal: Shoujun repeatedly followed armies in campaigns; before and after he suffered thirty-six wounds.
translations.idiomatic: Across many campaigns Shoujun had been wounded thirty-six times.

sentences.zh: 景德中，錄其子允慶為奉職。

translations.literal: In the Jingde era, his son Yunqing was entered on the register as a palace attendant.
translations.idiomatic: During the Jingde era his son Yunqing was granted palace attendant status.

sentences.zh: 弟守信，官崇儀副使；

translations.literal: His younger brother Shouxin held the office of deputy commissioner of honored ritual;
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Shouxin served as deputy commissioner of honored ritual;

sentences.zh: 守榮，內園使。

translations.literal: Shourong was an Inner Park envoy.
translations.idiomatic: his brother Shourong was an Inner Park envoy.

sentences.zh: 徐興，青州人。

translations.literal: Xu Xing was a native of Qingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Xing came from Qing prefecture.

sentences.zh: 以拳勇得隸兵籍。

translations.literal: Through boxing courage he obtained assignment to the military rolls.
translations.idiomatic: His prowess in boxing won him a place on the military rolls.

sentences.zh: 周顯德中，從太祖征淮右。

translations.literal: In the Xiande era of Zhou, he followed the Taizu in the campaign of the Huai Right.
translations.idiomatic: During the Xiande era he followed Taizu on the Huai River campaign.

sentences.zh: 宋初，隸御龍直。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Song, he was assigned to the Imperial Dragon Direct [Guard].
translations.idiomatic: At the dynasty's founding he joined the Imperial Dragon Guard.

sentences.zh: 會平澤、潞，上其功，補控鶴軍使。

translations.literal: When Ze and Lu were pacified, his merit was reported upward, and he was appointed officer of the Crane Control Army.
translations.idiomatic: When Ze and Lu prefectures were subdued, his feats were reported and he was made an officer of the Crane Control Army.

sentences.zh: 征晉陽，部卒壅汾水灌幷州城，益多其勞。

translations.literal: On the campaign against Jinyang, his subordinate troops dammed the Fen River to inundate the Bingzhou city walls, further increasing his labors.
translations.idiomatic: On the Jinyang expedition his men dammed the Fen River to flood the walls of Taiyuan, adding still more to his credit.

sentences.zh: 還，遷本軍副指揮使。

translations.literal: On return, he was promoted to deputy commander of his own army.
translations.idiomatic: After the campaign he was promoted to deputy commander of his corps.

sentences.zh: 太平興國初，從潘美趣團柏谷，奮與賊鬥，有果敢氣，人莫能勝。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Taiping Xingguo, he followed Pan Mei in pressing toward Tuanbo Valley, strove in battle with the rebels, had a daring and resolute spirit, and no one could overcome him.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Taiping Xingguo era he marched with Pan Mei toward Tuanbo Valley, fought the enemy with reckless valor, and carried such bold spirit that none could best him.

sentences.zh: 生擒偽兵馬都監李美，身被重創，無所回撓。

translations.literal: He captured alive the false state's horse-and-foot army supervisory commissioner Li Mei; his body received grave wounds, yet he yielded in nothing.
translations.idiomatic: He took the enemy horse-and-foot supervisor Li Mei alive; though grievously wounded, he did not flinch.

sentences.zh: 加指揮使。

translations.literal: He was advanced to army commander.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to corps commander.

sentences.zh: 太宗征太原，討幽、薊，興從戰，屢中流矢，以著跡聞。

translations.literal: When Emperor Taizong campaigned against Taiyuan and attacked You and Ji, Xing followed in battle, repeatedly being struck by stray arrows, and became known for his marks [of wounds].
translations.idiomatic: When Taizong campaigned against Taiyuan and against You and Ji, Xing fought in his train, took arrow after arrow, and won fame for the scars he carried.

sentences.zh: 補天武都虞候，累遷秩，出為洺州部署。

translations.literal: He was appointed chief adjutant of the Heavenly Martial [Guard], rose through repeated promotions in rank, and went out as deployment commissioner of Mingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He became chief adjutant of the Heavenly Martial Guard, rose through several promotions, and was posted as deployment commissioner of Mingzhou.

sentences.zh: 初議建方田，命興董其事，尋復輟。

translations.literal: When the square-field system was first debated for establishment, Xing was ordered to supervise the matter; soon it was again halted.
translations.idiomatic: When the court first debated establishing the square-field tax system, Xing was assigned to oversee it, but the project was soon abandoned.

sentences.zh: 端拱中，修鎮、定城，逾月訖工。

translations.literal: In the Duangong era, he repaired the cities of Zhen and Ding; within a month the work was completed.
translations.idiomatic: During the Duangong era (988–989) he rebuilt the walls of Zhen and Ding and finished within a month.

sentences.zh: 改莫州防禦使、知靜戎軍，歷祁、博二州。

translations.literal: He was changed to defense commissioner of Mozhou and administrator of Jingrong Army; he passed through the two prefectures of Qi and Bo.
translations.idiomatic: He was made defense commissioner of Mo prefecture and commandant of Jingrong Army, and later governed Qi and Bo prefectures.

sentences.zh: 咸平中，為涇、原、環、慶十州部署。

translations.literal: In the Xianping era, he was deployment commissioner of the ten prefectures of Jing, Yuan, Huan, and Qing.
translations.idiomatic: During the Xianping era he commanded deployment for the ten prefectures of Jing, Yuan, Huan, and Qing.

sentences.zh: 詔督轉靈武芻糧，道積石，率掠於寇。

translations.literal: By edict he supervised the transport of Lingwu fodder and grain; on the road at Jishi, the commander was plundered by the invaders.
translations.idiomatic: Ordered to convoy fodder for Lingwu along the Jishi route, he and his column were ambushed by the enemy.

sentences.zh: 興以步兵畏恧，戰不利，時王榮援兵不應，遂敗走。

translations.literal: Xing, because the foot soldiers were timid and fearful, did not fight well; at the time Wang Rong's relief troops did not respond, and so they were defeated and fled.
translations.idiomatic: His infantry fought poorly out of fear; when Wang Rong's reinforcements failed to come up, Xing was routed and driven off.

sentences.zh: 坐削籍，流郢州。

translations.literal: For the offense his name was struck from the rolls and he was banished to Yingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was stricken from the rolls and exiled to Yingzhou.

sentences.zh: 會赦，入為右衛將軍，遷左監門衛大將軍。

translations.literal: When an amnesty came, he entered court as general of the Right Guard and was promoted to great general of the Left Gate Guard Army.
translations.idiomatic: After a general amnesty he returned as a general of the Right Guard and was promoted to great general of the Left Gate Guard.

sentences.zh: 景德二年卒，年六十八。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jingde, he died, aged sixty-eight.
translations.idiomatic: He died in 1005 at the age of sixty-eight.

sentences.zh: 王杲，齊州人。

translations.literal: Wang Gao was a native of Qizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Gao came from Qi prefecture.

sentences.zh: 周顯德中，應募為卒。

translations.literal: In the Xiande era of Zhou, he answered recruitment as a soldier.
translations.idiomatic: During the Xiande era he enlisted as a common soldier.

sentences.zh: 從世宗收三關，隸先鋒。

translations.literal: He followed Emperor Shizong in the recovery of the Three Passes and was assigned to the vanguard.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Shizong in recovering the Three Passes and served in the vanguard.

sentences.zh: 宋初，征澤、潞，平揚州，杲應選從行，既獲戰功，乃拔遷散指揮使，累轉馬軍副都軍頭，屯幷州。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Song, on the campaigns against Ze and Lu and the pacification of Yangzhou, Gao was selected to follow in the march; having gained battle merit, he was then promoted and transferred to commander of the Loose [Retainer] command, repeatedly transferred to deputy chief of the horse army, and encamped at Bingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When the new dynasty campaigned in Ze and Lu and pacified Yangzhou, Gao marched with the armies; after distinguished service he was pulled up to commander of the Loose Retainer Guard, rose to deputy chief of the cavalry, and was stationed at Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 雍熙中，為龍衛右第二軍都虞候。

translations.literal: In the Yongxi era, he was chief adjutant of the Dragon Guard Right Second Army.
translations.idiomatic: During the Yongxi era he became chief adjutant of the second company of the right Dragon Guard.

sentences.zh: 會遣趙保忠還夏州，命杲引兵護送。

translations.literal: When Zhao Baozhong was sent back to Xiazhou, Gao was ordered to lead troops to escort him.
translations.idiomatic: When the court sent Zhao Baozhong back to Xiazhou, Gao was ordered to escort him with an armed column.

sentences.zh: 及還，保忠以方物贐，杲拒不納。

translations.literal: On the return, Baozhong offered local products as a bride-gift bribe; Gao refused and did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: On the return journey Baozhong offered him local gifts as a gratuity, but Gao refused them.

sentences.zh: 太宗知之，詔賜白金百兩。

translations.literal: Emperor Taizong learned of it and issued an edict bestowing one hundred taels of white gold.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong learned of his integrity and issued an edict awarding him one hundred taels of silver.

sentences.zh: 遷右第一軍，屯鎮州。

translations.literal: He was transferred to the Right First Army and encamped at Zhenzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was shifted to the first company of the right wing and stationed at Zhenzhou.

sentences.zh: 契丹入寇，隸大將郭守文，扞城，杲守北關。

translations.literal: When the Khitan invaded, he was assigned under Great General Guo Shouwen to defend the city; Gao guarded the north gate.
translations.idiomatic: When the Khitan invaded, he served under General Guo Shouwen in the defense of the city, holding the north gate.

sentences.zh: 寇退，命督餉藁趣威虜軍。

translations.literal: When the invaders withdrew, he was ordered to supervise the transport of fodder and rush it to the Weilu Army.
translations.idiomatic: After the raiders withdrew, he was ordered to supervise fodder shipments and hurry them to the Weilu garrison.

sentences.zh: 還抵徐河，時尹繼倫與寇戰，小衄，杲適遇賊河上，即按兵拒之，殺賊，奪所乘馬。

translations.literal: Returning, he reached the Xu River; at the time Yin Jilun was fighting the invaders and suffered a small setback; Gao happened to meet the bandits on the river, immediately halted his troops to resist them, killed the enemy, and seized the horse they had been riding.
translations.idiomatic: On the return march he reached the Xu River, where Yin Jilun was already fighting the raiders and had taken a minor setback. Gao happened upon the enemy at the river, held his men in place to block them, killed several, and captured their mounts.

sentences.zh: 守文上聞，得召見問狀，補都軍頭、領勤州刺史，命監河北，有能聲，尋命閱教定州諸軍騎射，入掌軍頭引見司。

translations.literal: Shouwen reported upward; he obtained a summons to audience to be questioned on the circumstances, was appointed chief of the army command and concurrently prefect of Qinzhou, ordered to supervise Hebei, gained a reputation for ability, and shortly afterward was ordered to inspect and drill the mounted archery of the various armies at Dingzhou, entering to take charge of the Army Chiefs Presentation Office.
