translations.idiomatic: Guo Shouwen reported his feat to the throne, and Gao was summoned to give an account of the fight. He was appointed chief army commander and acting prefect of Qinzhou, charged with oversight of Hebei, and soon won a name for efficiency. He was then ordered to review mounted archery drill for the Dingzhou garrisons and entered service in the office that presented army commanders to the emperor.

sentences.zh: 李順亂，與尹元並為西川招安使，敗賊，斬首萬級，以功真拜唐州刺史。

translations.literal: When Li Shun rebelled, he and Yin Yuan were jointly made pacification commissioners of West River, defeated the rebels, beheaded ten thousand at the ten-thousand level, and for his merit was formally appointed prefect of Tangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: During Li Shun's rebellion he served with Yin Yuan as pacification commissioner for the Sichuan basin, routed the rebels, and took ten thousand heads. For this he received a regular appointment as prefect of Tangzhou.

sentences.zh: 時賊雖平，道路尚梗，餘黨或保山林以肆姦，杲與石普等追捕於彭州，於是始平。

translations.literal: At the time, though the rebels were pacified, the roads were still blocked; remnant factions sometimes held the mountains and forests to commit outrages; Gao with Shi Pu and others pursued them at Pengzhou, and only then was order finally restored.
translations.idiomatic: Although the main rising had been crushed, communications were still unsafe and holdouts lurked in the hills. Gao, Shi Pu, and others hunted them down around Pengzhou, and only then was the region fully pacified.

sentences.zh: 至道初，乃還。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Zhidao era, he then returned.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of the Zhidao reign he returned to court.

sentences.zh: 復遷靈州副部署，道環州，留改幷州，徙知夏州。

translations.literal: He was again transferred to deputy commissioner at Lingzhou, passed through Huanzhou, was retained and reassigned to Bingzhou, and was moved to serve as prefect of Xiazhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was posted again as deputy commissioner at Lingzhou, traveled by way of Huanzhou, was kept on and reassigned to Taiyuan, and was then transferred to govern Xiazhou.

sentences.zh: 會趙保吉歸款，召還，次伏落津，移知石州，徙石、隰副部署。

translations.literal: When Zhao Baoji came over in submission, he was recalled, halted at Fuluo Ford, was reassigned to govern Shizhou, and was transferred to deputy commissioner of Shi and Xi.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhao Baoji submitted to the dynasty, Gao was recalled, paused at Fuluo Ford, was made prefect of Shizhou, and then became deputy commissioner for the Shi and Xi circuit.

sentences.zh: 未幾，以轉餉河西失期，降右千牛衛大將軍。

translations.literal: Before long, because the transport of provisions to Hexi missed its deadline, he was demoted to great general of the Right Palace Interior Service.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was demoted to great general of the Right Palace Interior Service for delivering Hexi supplies late.

sentences.zh: 咸平五年，出為亳州永城縣都監。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Xianping, he went out as chief supervisor of Yongcheng county in Bozhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Xianping he was sent out as chief military supervisor of Yongcheng county in Bozhou.

sentences.zh: 被召，將入見，以疾亟弗果，卒，年六十四。

translations.literal: He was summoned and was about to enter for audience, but because his illness was acute he did not succeed; he died, aged sixty-four.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned to court but his illness worsened before he could attend; he died at sixty-four.

sentences.zh: 李重誨

translations.literal: Li Zhonghui
translations.idiomatic: Li Zhonghui

sentences.zh: 李重誨，應州金城人。

translations.literal: Li Zhonghui was a native of Jincheng in Yingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Li Zhonghui came from Jincheng in Ying prefecture.

sentences.zh: 祖高，後唐莊宅使、獎州刺史。

translations.literal: His grandfather Gao was estate commissioner of Later Tang and prefect of Jiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Gao had served Later Tang as estate commissioner and as prefect of Jiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 父彥榮，仕契丹，署環州刺史，重誨嘗為其應州馬步軍都指揮使。

translations.literal: His father Yanrong served the Khitan, was appointed prefect of Huanzhou, and Zhonghui had once been his commander-in-chief of the Yingzhou horse and foot armies.
translations.idiomatic: His father Yanrong served the Khitan and held the prefecture of Huanzhou; Zhonghui had once commanded the combined horse and foot forces of Yingzhou under him.

sentences.zh: 太平興國五年，潘美出師禦寇，重誨從其節度使蕭咄李迎戰於代州北嶺，大敗。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Taiping Xingguo, Pan Mei led an army to repel invaders; Zhonghui followed his military commissioner Xiao Duoli to meet the enemy at North Ridge in Daizhou and suffered a great defeat.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Taiping Xingguo, Pan Mei marched out against the invaders. Zhonghui followed the Khitan commissioner Xiao Duoli to give battle at North Ridge in Daizhou and was routed.

sentences.zh: 美斬咄李，擒重誨以獻。

translations.literal: Mei beheaded Duoli and captured Zhonghui to present him.
translations.idiomatic: Pan Mei executed Xiao Duoli, captured Zhonghui, and sent him up as a prize.

sentences.zh: 太宗召見，補鄧州馬步軍都指揮使。

translations.literal: Emperor Taizong summoned him to audience and appointed him commander-in-chief of the Dengzhou horse and foot armies.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong received him at court and appointed him commander of the horse and foot forces at Dengzhou.

sentences.zh: 會趙普出鎮，奏監州軍。

translations.literal: When Zhao Pu went out to a frontier command, he memorialized to have Zhonghui supervise the prefectural army.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhao Pu took up a frontier post, he recommended Zhonghui to supervise the local garrison.

sentences.zh: 雍熙三年，召還，為武州刺史，出為忻州都巡檢、緣邊十八砦招安制置使，賜服帶、鞍馬。

translations.literal: In the third year of Yongxi, he was recalled, made prefect of Wuzhou, sent out as chief inspector of Xinzhou and pacification and disposition commissioner for the eighteen border stockades, and was granted court robes, belt, saddle, and horse.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Yongxi he was recalled, appointed prefect of Wuzhou, then sent out as chief inspector of Xinzhou and commissioner for pacifying the eighteen border forts, with court dress, belt, saddle, and horse as gifts.

sentences.zh: 北兵寇邊，重誨以所部邀戰，敗之，獲羊馬、鎧甲甚眾，賜詔嘉美。

translations.literal: Northern troops raided the border; Zhonghui with his command intercepted them in battle, defeated them, and captured a great many sheep, horses, and suits of armor; an edict was bestowed praising his merit.
translations.idiomatic: When northern forces raided the frontier, Zhonghui met them with his troops, routed them, and took large numbers of sheep, horses, and armor. The throne issued an edict of commendation.

sentences.zh: 會嶺蠻叛，改廣、桂、融、宜、柳州招安捉賊使，聽便宜從事。

translations.literal: When the hill barbarians rebelled, he was changed to pacification and bandit-capture commissioner for Guang, Gui, Rong, Yi, and Liuzhou, with authority to act as circumstances required.
translations.idiomatic: When the hill tribes rebelled, he was reassigned as pacification and bandit-suppression commissioner for Guang, Gui, Rong, Yi, and Liuzhou, with discretionary authority.

sentences.zh: 至道初，累遷涇原儀渭鎮戎軍鈐轄。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhidao, he was repeatedly transferred to supervisory commissioner of the Jingyuan, Yiwei, and Zhenrong armies.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of the Zhidao reign he rose to supervisory commissioner over the Jingyuan, Yiwei, and Zhenrong commands.

sentences.zh: 咸平三年，徙邠寧環慶路。

translations.literal: In the third year of Xianping, he was moved to the Binning-Huanqing circuit.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Xianping he was transferred to the Binning-Huanqing frontier circuit.

sentences.zh: 坐轉餉靈武不嚴斥候，至積石為虜騎掠於道，營部大亂，除名，流光州。

translations.literal: He was punished because, while transporting provisions to Lingwu, he did not strictly maintain scouts; when he reached Jishi, he was plundered on the road by barbarian cavalry, the camp fell into great disorder, his name was struck from the rolls, and he was banished to Guangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was cashiered for lax scouting while convoying supplies to Lingwu: at Jishi barbarian horsemen fell upon his column on the road, his camp broke in disorder, his name was struck from the rolls, and he was exiled to Guangzhou.

sentences.zh: 五年，起為內殿崇班、鄜延駐泊都監，俄遷崇儀使。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, he was raised to palace interior aide and chief supervisor of the garrison at Yan'an on the Yan circuit, and shortly afterward was transferred to commissioner of honored ceremony.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he was restored as palace interior aide and chief supervisor of the Yan'an garrison on the Yan circuit, and soon promoted to commissioner of honored ceremony.

sentences.zh: 景德中，趙德明既納款，或言以麟、府謀有他志。

translations.literal: In the Jingde era, after Zhao Deming had submitted, some said that with Lin and Fu he harbored other designs.
translations.idiomatic: During the Jingde era, after Zhao Deming had submitted, some claimed he was plotting mischief with the prefectures of Lin and Fu.

sentences.zh: 上以涇原地要兵眾，慮有緩急，遂徙重誨為鈐轄。

translations.literal: The emperor, because the Jingyuan region was strategically vital and its troops numerous, feared an emergency and therefore transferred Zhonghui there as supervisory commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, judging the Jingyuan frontier both vital and heavily garrisoned and fearing a sudden crisis, moved Zhonghui there as supervisory commissioner.

sentences.zh: 復遷益州，改皇城使。

translations.literal: He was again transferred to Yizhou and changed to commissioner of the Imperial City.
translations.idiomatic: He was later transferred to Yizhou and made commissioner of the Imperial City.

sentences.zh: 大中祥符六年，卒，年六十八。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Dazhong Xiangfu, he died, aged sixty-eight.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Dazhong Xiangfu he died at sixty-eight.

sentences.zh: 重誨純愨寡過。

translations.literal: Zhonghui was pure, sincere, and seldom at fault.
translations.idiomatic: Zhonghui was upright, dutiful, and seldom in error.

sentences.zh: 真宗悼其沒於遠土，命其子乘傳往護柩歸，聽止驛舍之別次。

translations.literal: Emperor Zhenzong grieved that he had died in distant territory and ordered his son to travel by relay post to escort the coffin home, permitting him to lodge at the separate quarters of post stations.
translations.idiomatic: Zhenzong grieved that he had died so far from home and ordered his son to travel by imperial relay to escort the coffin back, with permission to use the private quarters at post stations along the way.

sentences.zh: 子禹謨，錄為將作監主簿。

translations.literal: His son Yumou was entered on the rolls as master of records in the Directorate of Works.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yumou was granted a registry appointment as master of records in the Directorate of Works.

sentences.zh: 弟重睿，歷官澄州團練使。

translations.literal: His younger brother Zhongrui rose through office to regimental commissioner of Chengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Zhongrui eventually became regimental commissioner of Chengzhou.

sentences.zh: 子禹偁，閤門祗候。

translations.literal: His son Yucheng was a gate attendant of the Privy Chamber.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yucheng served as a Privy Chamber gate attendant.

sentences.zh: 白守素

translations.literal: Bai Shousu
translations.idiomatic: Bai Shousu

sentences.zh: 白守素，開封人。

translations.literal: Bai Shousu was a native of Kaifeng.
translations.idiomatic: Bai Shousu came from Kaifeng.

sentences.zh: 祖延遇，仕周至鎮國軍節度。

translations.literal: His grandfather Yanyu served Zhou and rose to military commissioner of the Zhenguo Army.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Yanyu had served the Later Zhou and risen to military commissioner of the Zhenguo army.

sentences.zh: 父廷訓，宋初為龍捷都指揮使、領博州刺史。

translations.literal: His father Tingxun, at the beginning of Song, was commander of the Dragon Swift command and concurrently prefect of Bozhou.
translations.idiomatic: His father Tingxun, in the early Song, commanded the Dragon Swift Guard and concurrently governed Bozhou.

sentences.zh: 守素以蔭補東班承旨。

translations.literal: Shousu, by hereditary privilege, was appointed attendant of the Eastern Shift.
translations.idiomatic: Shousu entered service by hereditary privilege as an attendant of the Eastern Shift.

sentences.zh: 太平興國五年，遷補右班殿直，以善射，授供奉官、帶御器械，三遷至供備庫使。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Taiping Xingguo, he was transferred and appointed palace interior aide of the Right Shift; because of skill in archery, he was made tribute officer and bearer of imperial arms, and after three promotions reached commissioner of the Supply Repository.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Taiping Xingguo he was promoted to palace interior aide of the Right Shift. His marksmanship won him appointment as tribute officer and bearer of imperial arms, and three further promotions brought him to commissioner of the Supply Repository.

sentences.zh: 咸平三年春，契丹犯邊，命與王能戍邢州，俄又與麥守恩、石贊領先鋒禦之。

translations.literal: In the spring of the third year of Xianping, the Khitan raided the border; he was ordered with Wang Neng to garrison Xingzhou, and shortly afterward with Mai Shou'en and Shi Zan to lead the vanguard in defense.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the third year of Xianping, when the Khitan raided the frontier, he was ordered with Wang Neng to hold Xingzhou and soon afterward joined Mai Shou'en and Shi Zan in leading the vanguard against them.

sentences.zh: 敵退，復與荊嗣督河北、京東捕賊。

translations.literal: When the enemy withdrew, he again with Jing Si supervised the capture of bandits in Hebei and Jingdong.
translations.idiomatic: After the enemy withdrew, he joined Jing Si in supervising bandit suppression in Hebei and the eastern capital region.

sentences.zh: 四年，命為鎮州行營鈐轄，領騎兵攝大陣西偏，屢當格鬥。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, he was appointed supervisory commissioner of the field headquarters at Zhenzhou, leading cavalry and acting for the western wing of the great battle line, repeatedly meeting hand-to-hand combat.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he was made supervisory commissioner of the Zhenzhou field headquarters, commanding cavalry on the army's western wing and repeatedly fighting at close quarters.

sentences.zh: 俄改定州鈐轄，復徙鎮州。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward he was changed to supervisory commissioner at Dingzhou and again transferred to Zhenzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon reassigned as supervisory commissioner at Dingzhou, then transferred back to Zhenzhou.

sentences.zh: 王繼忠之陷也，宋師還渡河，敵人乘之，守素據橋，有矢數百，每發必中，敵不敢近，遂引去。

translations.literal: When Wang Jizhong was captured, the Song army returned and crossed the river; the enemy pursued them; Shousu held the bridge with several hundred arrows, every shot hitting its mark; the enemy did not dare approach and therefore withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: After Wang Jizhong's capture the Song army recrossed the river with the enemy in pursuit. Shousu held the bridge with several hundred arrows and never missed; the pursuers dared not close and drew off.

sentences.zh: 真宗與輔臣議三路禦賊，咸曰：「威虜扼北道要害尤甚，請分騎兵六千屯之，命魏能為部署。」

translations.literal: Emperor Zhenzong discussed with chief ministers the defense against bandits on the three routes; all said: "Weilu especially chokes the vital point of the northern road; we request that six thousand cavalry be detached to encamp there and Wei Neng be appointed commissioner."
translations.idiomatic: Zhenzong discussed frontier defense with his chief ministers. All agreed: "Weilu guards the most critical point on the northern route. We recommend posting six thousand cavalry there under Wei Neng as commissioner."

sentences.zh: 上曰：「能頗強愎，尤難共事，聞守素久練邊計，張銳性頗和善，參知戎務，庶克相濟。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Neng is rather forceful and obstinate and especially hard to work with; I have heard that Shousu has long practiced frontier strategy and Zhang Rui's nature is rather mild and agreeable; let them jointly manage military affairs, and perhaps they can assist one another."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor replied: "Neng is headstrong and notoriously difficult. Shousu, I am told, has long experience on the frontier, and Zhang Rui is mild by nature. If they share military duties, they may balance one another."

sentences.zh: 乃命守素、銳為鈐轄，戍順安以貳之。

translations.literal: He then appointed Shousu and Rui supervisory commissioners, garrisoning Shun'an as deputies to him.
translations.idiomatic: He therefore appointed Shousu and Zhang Rui supervisory commissioners and stationed them at Shun'an as Neng's deputies.

sentences.zh: 景德元年，契丹侵長城口，守素與能發兵破之，追北過陽山，斬首級、獲器械甚眾，賜錦袍、金帶。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jingde, when the Khitan invaded Changcheng Pass, Shousu and Neng led troops and defeated them, pursued north beyond Yangshan, beheaded many at the head-count, and seized a great quantity of equipment; he was granted a brocade robe and gold belt.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Jingde (1004), when the Khitan attacked Changcheng Pass, Shousu and Wang Neng routed them, pursued them north beyond Yangshan, took many heads, and captured large stores of equipment. He was rewarded with a brocade robe and gold belt.

sentences.zh: 俄徙屯冀州，轉運使劉綜舉其智勇，材任將帥，加領康州刺史。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to encamp at Jizhou; transport commissioner Liu Zong commended his wisdom and courage and his talent fit for command, and he was additionally given the prefecture of Kangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon shifted to garrison Jizhou. Transport commissioner Liu Zong praised his intelligence and valor and recommended him as general material, and he was additionally made prefect of Kangzhou.

sentences.zh: 又提騎卒戍靜戎軍，兼蒞營田之役，俄為鎮、定鈐轄。

translations.literal: He again led cavalry to garrison Jingrong Army, concurrently overseeing agricultural garrison duties, and soon became supervisory commissioner of Zhen and Ding.
translations.idiomatic: He next led cavalry to garrison Jingrong Army while also supervising military farming, and was soon made supervisory commissioner of Zhen and Ding.

sentences.zh: 是冬，契丹復內侵，守素敗其前鋒，獲車重，又入敵境，俘擒眾從。

translations.literal: That winter the Khitan again invaded inland; Shousu defeated their vanguard, seized baggage trains, again entered enemy territory, and captured many followers.
translations.idiomatic: That winter, when the Khitan invaded again, Shousu routed their vanguard, seized supply trains, pressed into enemy territory, and took many prisoners.

sentences.zh: 及請和，省邊戍之職，與曹璨留任鎮、定。

translations.literal: When peace was requested, frontier garrison posts were reduced; he and Cao Can remained in office at Zhen and Ding.
translations.idiomatic: After peace was sought, frontier garrisons were reduced, and he and Cao Can remained in command at Zhen and Ding.

sentences.zh: 追敘前勞，加合州團練使。

translations.literal: His earlier labors were recounted and rewarded, and he was advanced to regimental commissioner of Hezhou.
translations.idiomatic: His earlier service was formally recognized and he was promoted to regimental commissioner of Hezhou.

sentences.zh: 大中祥符三年，命副李迪使契丹。

translations.literal: In the third year of Dazhong Xiangfu, he was ordered as deputy to Li Di on an embassy to the Khitan.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Dazhong Xiangfu he was ordered to accompany Li Di as deputy envoy to the Khitan court.

sentences.zh: 守素居邊歲久，名聞北庭，頗畏伏之。

translations.literal: Shousu had dwelt on the border many years; his name was known in the northern court, and they rather feared and submitted to him.
translations.idiomatic: Shousu had served on the frontier for many years, and his name was well known in the northern court, where he was widely feared.

sentences.zh: 上慮其不欲行，密遣內侍詢於守素，守素頓首感咽，即以崔可道代焉。

translations.literal: The emperor feared he did not wish to go and secretly sent a palace attendant to inquire of Shousu; Shousu bowed his head and wept with emotion, and thereupon Cui Kedao was substituted in his place.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor feared he was unwilling to leave the frontier and secretly sent a palace attendant to ask him. Shousu bowed to the ground in tears, and Cui Kedao was sent in his stead.

sentences.zh: 再遷南作坊使。

translations.literal: He was again transferred to commissioner of the Southern Works.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted again to commissioner of the Southern Works.

sentences.zh: 大中祥符五年，卒。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Dazhong Xiangfu, he died.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Dazhong Xiangfu he died.

sentences.zh: 上甚惜之，常賻外別賚錢五十萬，令護喪還京師，錄其一子官。

translations.literal: The emperor greatly regretted it; beyond the usual funeral gifts he separately bestowed five hundred thousand in cash, ordered him to escort the coffin back to the capital, and entered one of his sons on the official rolls.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor deeply mourned his loss, granted fifty thousand strings of cash beyond the usual funeral gifts, ordered his coffin escorted to the capital, and enrolled one of his sons in office.

sentences.zh: 張思鈞

translations.literal: Zhang Sijun
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Sijun

sentences.zh: 張思鈞，邢州沙河人。

translations.literal: Zhang Sijun was a native of Shahe in Xingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Sijun came from Shahe in Xing prefecture.

sentences.zh: 祖中正，漢澤州刺史。

translations.literal: His grandfather Zhongzheng was prefect of Zezhou under Han.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Zhongzheng had been prefect of Zezhou under the Later Han.

sentences.zh: 思鈞少善擊劍、挽強，善博奕。

translations.literal: Sijun in youth was skilled at swordplay and drawing the strong bow and was adept at gambling.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth Sijun excelled at swordplay and the heavy bow and was fond of gambling.

sentences.zh: 初應募為卒，晉開運間，遷廣銳軍使。

translations.literal: At first he answered recruitment as a soldier; in the Kaiyun era of Jin, he was transferred to commander of the Broad Sharp army.
translations.idiomatic: He first enlisted as a common soldier and, during the Jin Kaiyun era, rose to command the Broad Sharp army.

sentences.zh: 周廣順初，從聶知遇攻河東，破其眾三千餘。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Guangshun of Zhou, he served under Nie Zhiyu in attacking Hedong and broke more than three thousand of their troops.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of the Zhou Guangshun reign he followed Nie Zhiyu against Hedong and routed more than three thousand of the enemy.

sentences.zh: 從向訓東征，為捉生將，擒小校張萬於江豬嶺。

translations.literal: He followed Xiang Xun on the eastern campaign, served as a captive-taking officer, and captured the junior officer Zhang Wan at Jiangzhu Ridge.
translations.idiomatic: He marched east with Xiang Xun as a captive-taking officer and seized the junior officer Zhang Wan at Jiangzhu Ridge.

sentences.zh: 又從符彥卿與幷人鬥代州，留為南北兩關巡檢。

translations.literal: He again followed Fu Yanqing in fighting the Bing men at Daizhou and was retained as inspector of the northern and southern passes.
translations.idiomatic: He then followed Fu Yanqing in fighting the Taiyuan forces at Daizhou and was left as inspector of the northern and southern passes.

sentences.zh: 宋初，補龍衛指揮使。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Song, he was appointed commander of the Dragon Guard.
translations.idiomatic: When the Song dynasty was founded he was appointed commander of the Dragon Guard.

sentences.zh: 李繼勳下遼州，戰帶甲祠，斬首萬餘級，追奔至長城，擒其將莫山、鮑淑，掠人騎二百餘。

translations.literal: When Li Jixun descended on Liaozhou, he fought at the Armored Shrine, beheaded more than ten thousand, pursued the rout to the Long Wall, captured their generals Mo Shan and Bao Shu, and seized more than two hundred men and horses.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Jixun marched on Liaozhou, Sijun fought at the Armored Shrine, took more than ten thousand heads, pursued the fugitives to the Long Wall, captured the generals Mo Shan and Bao Shu, and seized more than two hundred men and mounts.

sentences.zh: 俄屯潞州，合戰三十餘。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward he encamped at Luzhou and joined in more than thirty battles.
translations.idiomatic: He soon encamped at Luzhou and took part in more than thirty engagements.

sentences.zh: 乾德中，以勞秩遷都虞候。

translations.literal: In the Qiande era, for merit in rank he was transferred to chief adjutant.
translations.idiomatic: During the Qiande era he was promoted to chief adjutant for his service.

sentences.zh: 開寶三年，郭進、田欽祚戍三交，嘗從戰於石嶺關，斬首萬五千餘級。

translations.literal: In the third year of Kaibao, Guo Jin and Tian Qinhuo garrisoned Sanjiao; he once followed in battle at Shiling Pass and beheaded more than fifteen thousand.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Kaibao, when Guo Jin and Tian Qinhuo held Sanjiao, he fought with them at Shiling Pass and took more than fifteen thousand heads.

sentences.zh: 閤門祗候齊延琛、苗昶陷軍中，思鈞鼓勁騎突入，奪還。

translations.literal: The Privy Chamber attendants Qi Yanchen and Miao Chang were trapped in the army; Sijun roused crack cavalry and charged in, seizing them back.
translations.idiomatic: When the Privy Chamber attendants Qi Yanchen and Miao Chang were cut off in the field, Sijun led crack horsemen in a charge and brought them out.

sentences.zh: 何繼筠入晉境，思鈞隸麾下，拔南橋徑度。

translations.literal: When He Jiyun entered Jin territory, Sijun was under his command, stormed South Bridge, and passed straight through.
translations.idiomatic: When He Jiyun invaded Jin territory, Sijun served under him, stormed South Bridge, and broke through.

sentences.zh: 大將之出，必辟為先鋒。

translations.literal: Whenever great generals went out, they invariably selected him as vanguard.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever a senior commander took the field, Sijun was chosen as vanguard.

sentences.zh: 太平興國初，屯定州，領兵援磁窯，戰敗其眾，身中五十創，奮不顧，乃逐賊，薄軍城，奪馬及鎧甲居多。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Taiping Xingguo, he encamped at Dingzhou, led troops to relieve Ciyao, defeated their force, received fifty wounds on his body, fought on without regard, then pursued the bandits, pressed close to the army city, and seized a great many horses and suits of armor.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Taiping Xingguo era he was stationed at Dingzhou and marched to relieve Ciyao, routing the enemy though he took fifty wounds and fought on without pause. He drove the raiders to the walls of their stronghold and captured a great quantity of horses and armor.

sentences.zh: 未幾，邊人復攻，逆戰城下，斬首萬餘級。

translations.literal: Before long, border men attacked again; he met them in battle below the city and beheaded more than ten thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward the frontier enemy attacked again; he met them beneath the walls and took more than ten thousand heads.

sentences.zh: 上嘉之，命賜服帶，領河州刺史。

translations.literal: The emperor commended him and ordered court robes and belt bestowed; he concurrently held the prefecture of Hezhou.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor praised his valor, granted him court dress and belt, and appointed him acting prefect of Hezhou.

sentences.zh: 雍熙三年，邊人寇河間，劉廷讓會戰君子館，命思鈞翼從。

translations.literal: In the third year of Yongxi, border men raided Hejian; Liu Tingrang joined battle at the Gentleman's Lodge and ordered Sijun to flank and follow.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Yongxi, when frontier forces raided Hejian, Liu Tingrang gave battle at the Gentleman's Lodge and ordered Sijun to serve on his flank.

sentences.zh: 時天大寒，弓不得彀，援兵不至，於是敗績，陷留軍中數年，役役不得還。

translations.literal: At the time the heavens were bitterly cold, bows could not be drawn, and relief troops did not arrive; thereupon they were defeated, trapped and detained in the enemy army for several years, toiling without being able to return.
translations.idiomatic: The weather was bitterly cold, bows could not be drawn, and no reinforcements came. The army was routed, and Sijun spent years as a captive in Khitan hands, unable to return.

sentences.zh: 端拱初，自契丹始逃歸，授澄州刺史、知齊州。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Duangong, he first escaped and returned from the Khitan, was appointed prefect of Chengzhou, and was made administrator of Qizhou.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of the Duangong reign he escaped from Khitan captivity, was appointed prefect of Chengzhou, and was made administrator of Qizhou.

sentences.zh: 思鈞以武進，素不知民政，僅踰月，即徙濮、鄆、濱、棣州巡檢。

translations.literal: Sijun had risen through martial merit and from of old did not know civil administration; after barely more than a month, he was transferred to inspector of Pu, Yan, Bin, and Di prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: Sijun had risen by arms and knew nothing of civil government; after barely a month he was shifted to inspector over Pu, Yan, Bin, and Di prefectures.

sentences.zh: 至道中，改鄜延巡檢使。

translations.literal: In the Zhidao era, he was changed to inspector commissioner of the Yan circuit.
translations.idiomatic: During the Zhidao era he became inspector commissioner on the Yan frontier.

sentences.zh: 會葺右堡砦，擊寇走之。

translations.literal: When the Right Fort stockade was being repaired, he struck the raiders and drove them off.
translations.idiomatic: While the Right Fort stockade was under repair, he attacked the raiders and drove them off.

sentences.zh: 未幾，寇逼保安軍，與曹璨往援，追躡五十餘里，至木場，寇乃遁去。

translations.literal: Before long, raiders pressed Bao'an Army; with Cao Shen he went to relieve it, pursued for more than fifty li to Mucang, and the raiders then fled away.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward raiders threatened Bao'an Army. Sijun marched with Cao Shen to its relief, pursued them more than fifty li to Mucang, and the enemy withdrew.

sentences.zh: 真宗即位，徙益州鈐轄兼綿、漢九州都巡檢使。

translations.literal: When Emperor Zhenzong took the throne, he was transferred to supervisory commissioner of Yizhou and concurrently chief inspector of the nine prefectures of Mian and Han.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhenzong ascended the throne, Sijun was made supervisory commissioner of Yizhou and chief inspector of the nine prefectures of Mian and Han.

sentences.zh: 咸平中，以王均之亂，出兵保綿州。

translations.literal: In the Xianping era, because of Wang Jun's rebellion, he led troops out to defend Mianzhou.
translations.idiomatic: During the Xianping era, when Wang Jun rebelled, he marched out to hold Mianzhou.

sentences.zh: 賊陷漢州，思鈞進攻，克之，斬偽刺史苗進，又與石普敗賊彌牟砦。

translations.literal: When the rebels took Hanzhou, Sijun advanced to attack, captured it, beheaded the false prefect Miao Jin, and again with Shi Pu defeated the rebels at Miyu stockade.
translations.idiomatic: When the rebels seized Hanzhou, Sijun attacked, took the city, and executed the rebel prefect Miao Jin. He and Shi Pu then routed the rebels at Miyu stockade.

sentences.zh: 巴西尉傅翱有善馬，思鈞求之，翱不與。

translations.literal: Fu Ao, assistant magistrate of Baxi, had an excellent horse; Sijun requested it, but Ao would not give it.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Ao, assistant magistrate of Baxi, owned a fine horse that Sijun demanded; Fu Ao refused.

sentences.zh: 思鈞平賊，心恃功居多，召翱至，責以轉餉後期，斬之。

translations.literal: After Sijun pacified the rebels, in his heart he relied on his great merit; he summoned Ao, charged him with delivering provisions late, and beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: After pacifying the rebellion, Sijun, swollen with his own merit, summoned Fu Ao, accused him of late delivery of supplies, and executed him.

sentences.zh: 上聞其事，傳召付御史臺鞫治，罪當斬，特貸之，削籍流封州。

translations.literal: When the emperor heard of the affair, he had him summoned by relay and handed over to the Censorate for investigation and punishment; the crime merited execution, but he was specially pardoned, struck from the rolls, and banished to Fengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor learned of it, he had Sijun summoned to court and handed over to the Censorate. The offense warranted death, but he was spared, struck from the rolls, and exiled to Fengzhou.

sentences.zh: 六年，起為左司禦率府率、考城監軍。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, he was raised to colonel of the Left Bureau of the Imperial Guard and military supervisor of Kaocheng.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he was restored as colonel of the Left Bureau of the Imperial Guard and military supervisor of Kaocheng.

sentences.zh: 車駕幸澶淵，召詣行在，命李繼隆、石保吉同議兵事，賜服御有加。

translations.literal: When the imperial carriage visited Chanyuan, he was summoned to the traveling palace, ordered with Li Jilong and Shi Baoji jointly to discuss military affairs, and was granted additional court dress and accoutrements.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor went to Chanyuan, Sijun was summoned to the camp and ordered with Li Jilong and Shi Baoji to deliberate on military affairs, with extra gifts of court dress.

sentences.zh: 景德二年，為西京水北都巡檢使，俄分司西京。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jingde, he was chief inspector north of the river at the Western Capital, and shortly afterward held a separate commission at the Western Capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Jingde he became chief inspector north of the river at Luoyang and soon held a separate commission there.

sentences.zh: 召對行在，上憫其老，授唐州防禦副使，徙鄭州。

translations.literal: He was summoned to audience at the traveling palace; the emperor pitied his age and appointed him deputy commissioner of defense at Tangzhou, then transferred him to Zhengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Summoned to audience at the imperial camp, he was pitied for his age, appointed deputy commissioner of defense at Tangzhou, and transferred to Zhengzhou.

sentences.zh: 大中祥待二年，再遷左千牛衛將軍。

translations.literal: In the second year of Dazhong Xiangfu, he was again transferred to general of the Left Palace Interior Service.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Dazhong Xiangfu he was promoted again to general of the Left Palace Interior Service.

sentences.zh: 四年七月，卒，年八十九。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the fourth year, he died, aged eighty-nine.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of the fourth year he died at eighty-nine.

sentences.zh: 子承恩，為三班奉職。

translations.literal: His son Chengen was a third-rank service officer.
translations.idiomatic: His son Chengen held office as a third-rank service officer.

sentences.zh: 思鈞起行伍，征討稍有功。

translations.literal: Sijun rose from the ranks; in campaigns he had some slight merit.
translations.idiomatic: Sijun had risen from the ranks and won modest distinction in the field.

sentences.zh: 質狀小而精悍，太宗嘗稱其「樓羅」，自是人目為「小樓羅」焉。

translations.literal: His physique was small yet keen and hardy; Emperor Taizong once called him "Luo Lou," and from then on people regarded him as the "Little Luo Lou."
translations.idiomatic: Small in stature but fierce and quick, he was once called "Luo Lou" by Taizong, and thereafter men knew him as "Little Luo Lou."

sentences.zh: 李琪，河南伊闕人。

translations.literal: Li Qi was a native of Yique in Henan.
translations.idiomatic: Li Qi came from Yique in Henan.

sentences.zh: 幼生長兵家，得給事宣祖，左右太祖，以材力稱，進備執御。

translations.literal: From youth he grew up in a military household, obtained service attending the dynastic founder, attended at the left and right of Emperor Taizu, was famed for strength and ability, and was advanced to prepare and hold the imperial reins.
translations.idiomatic: He grew up in a military family, entered service under the dynastic founder, attended Taizu, won renown for strength and skill, and rose to serve in the imperial guard.

sentences.zh: 及受禪，命補鎮職。

translations.literal: When the throne was received, he was ordered to fill a garrison post.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizu took the throne, he was appointed to a frontier garrison post.

sentences.zh: 太宗在京府，復令事之。

translations.literal: When Taizong was in the capital prefecture, he was again ordered to attend him.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizong held the capital prefecture, he was again assigned to attend him.

sentences.zh: 由是累遷效忠都虞候、開封府馬步軍副都指揮使、領富州刺史。

translations.literal: Thereupon he was repeatedly promoted to chief adjutant of the Xiaozhong [Loyal Service] command, deputy commander-in-chief of the Kaifeng prefectural horse and foot armies, and concurrently prefect of Fuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through successive promotions to chief adjutant of the Loyal Service Guard, deputy commander-in-chief of the Kaifeng horse and foot forces, and prefect of Fuzhou.

sentences.zh: 嘗請對，自言經事太祖，而京師無居宅，太宗以官第假之。

translations.literal: He once requested an audience, stating himself that he had long served Taizu yet had no residence in the capital; Taizong lent him an official mansion.
translations.idiomatic: On one audience he noted that he had served Taizu from the beginning yet owned no house in the capital; Taizong lent him an official residence.

sentences.zh: 琪性素鄙，歷事三朝，而行不加修。

translations.literal: Qi's nature had always been base; he served through three reigns yet did not improve his conduct.
translations.idiomatic: Qi had always been coarse in character; though he served three reigns, he never improved his conduct.

sentences.zh: 每分遣士卒守護關梁，必覬其贈遺，視所厚薄為重輕。

translations.literal: Whenever he dispatched soldiers to guard passes and bridges, he always coveted their gifts and gauged importance by how generous they were.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he sent troops to guard passes and bridges, he coveted their gifts and treated people according to how much they gave.

sentences.zh: 太宗知之，遂改授屯衛大將軍，領郡如故，乃顧曰：「吾欲置琪於無過之地爾。」

translations.literal: Taizong learned of this and therefore changed his appointment to great general of the Garrison Guard while he retained his prefecture as before; he then looked back and said, "I wish to place Qi where he cannot err."
translations.idiomatic: When Taizong learned of this, he transferred Qi to great general of the Garrison Guard while letting him keep his prefecture, and remarked, "I mean to put Qi where he cannot get into trouble."

sentences.zh: 加左武衛大將軍。

translations.literal: He was advanced to great general of the Left Martial Guard.
translations.idiomatic: He was further promoted to great general of the Left Martial Guard.

sentences.zh: 景德中，以老且病，表求五日一赴起居，俄為臺諫所糾，令赴常參。

translations.literal: During Jingde, because he was old and ill, he memorialized requesting to attend court levee once every five days; soon censorial remonstrators impeached him and ordered him to attend regular court sessions.
translations.idiomatic: During the Jingde era, old and ill, he asked permission to attend court levee only once every five days. Censors soon impeached him and required regular attendance.

sentences.zh: 真宗念其舊，特賜給月奉以養。

translations.literal: Zhenzong, mindful of his long service, specially granted him a monthly stipend for his support.
translations.idiomatic: Zhenzong, remembering his long service, granted him a special monthly stipend for his upkeep.

sentences.zh: 大中祥符元年卒，年八十四。

translations.literal: In the first year of Dazhong Xiangfu he died, aged eighty-four.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the first year of Dazhong Xiangfu (1008) at the age of eighty-four.

sentences.zh: 王延範

translations.literal: Wang Yanfan
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yanfan

sentences.zh: 王延範，江陵人。

translations.literal: Wang Yanfan was a native of Jiangling.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yanfan was from Jiangling.

sentences.zh: 形貌奇偉，喜任俠，家富於財。

translations.literal: His appearance was strange and imposing; he delighted in chivalrous adventure, and his family was rich in wealth.
translations.idiomatic: He was striking in appearance, loved bold and chivalrous exploits, and came from a wealthy family.

sentences.zh: 父保義，為荊南高氏行軍司馬兼領武泰軍留後。

translations.literal: His father Baoyi served the Gao house of Jingnan as campaigning marshal and concurrently held the regency of the Wutai Army.
translations.idiomatic: His father Baoyi had served the Gao regime of Jingnan as campaigning marshal and acting regent of the Wutai Army.

sentences.zh: 高從誨奏署延範太子舍人。

translations.literal: Gao Conghui memorialized to appoint Yanfan as attendant of the heir apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Conghui had him appointed attendant in the heir apparent's household.

sentences.zh: 後隨從誨孫繼冲入覲，薦為大理寺丞、知泰州累遷司門員外郎。

translations.literal: Later he followed Conghui's grandson Jichong to court audience, was recommended as vice-director of the Court of Judicial Review and administrator of Taizhou, and was repeatedly promoted to outer-section vice-director of the Department of Gates.
translations.idiomatic: He later accompanied Gao Conghui's grandson Jichong to an audience at court, was recommended as a vice-director of the Court of Judicial Review and prefect of Taizhou, and rose to outer-section vice-director of the Department of Gates.

sentences.zh: 太平興國九年，為廣南轉運使。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Taiping Xingguo he was made transport commissioner of Guangnan.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year of Taiping Xingguo (984) he was appointed transport commissioner of Guangnan.

sentences.zh: 性豪率尚氣，尤好術數。

translations.literal: By nature he was bold, forthright, and spirited, and especially fond of occult calculations.
translations.idiomatic: He was bold, impulsive, and proud by nature, with a special fondness for divination and occult arts.

sentences.zh: 嘗通判梓州，有杜先生以左道惑眾，謂延範曰：「汝意有所之，我常陰為之助。」

translations.literal: He once served as co-administrator of Zizhou; a Master Du deluded the masses with heterodox ways and said to Yanfan, "Whatever you intend, I shall secretly aid you."
translations.idiomatic: While serving as co-administrator of Zizhou, a Master Du won followers through heterodox practices and told Yanfan, "Whatever you aim to do, I will secretly help you achieve it."

sentences.zh: 延範心喜，敢為恣橫。

translations.literal: Yanfan was delighted in heart and dared to act willfully and overbearingly.
translations.idiomatic: Heartened by this, Yanfan grew reckless and overbearing in his conduct.

sentences.zh: 後為江南轉運使，有劉昴賣卜於吉州市，其言多驗，謂延範曰：「公當偏霸一方。」

translations.literal: Later, as transport commissioner of Jiangnan, there was a Liu Mao who sold divinations in Jizhou city; his words mostly proved true, and he said to Yanfan, "Your Excellency ought to hold regional sway over one corner."
translations.idiomatic: Later, as Jiangnan transport commissioner, he met Liu Mao, a fortune-teller in Jizhou whose predictions often came true. Liu told him, "You are destined to rule a region in your own right."

sentences.zh: 又有徐肇為延範推九宮算法，得八少一，肇驚起曰：「君侯大貴不可言，當如江南李國主。」

translations.literal: There was also Xu Zhao, who for Yanfan worked the Nine Palaces algorithm and obtained eight short of one; Zhao started up in alarm and said, "My lord's great nobility cannot be spoken—you ought to be like Li the ruler of Jiangnan."
translations.idiomatic: Xu Zhao also cast the Nine Palaces divination for him and obtained eight short of the highest number. Xu exclaimed, "Your fortune is beyond words—you will rank with Li Yu of Jiangnan."

sentences.zh: 前戎城主簿田辨自言善相，謂延範曰：「君是坐天王形、頻伽眼、仙人鼻、雌龍耳、虎望，有大威德，猛烈富貴之相也。

translations.literal: The former registrar of Rongcheng, Tian Bian, declared himself skilled at physiognomy and said to Yanfan, "My lord has the form of a seated heavenly king, the eyes of a kalavinka, the nose of an immortal, the ears of a female dragon, and the gaze of a tiger—bearing great majesty and virtue, a physiognomy of fierce and noble wealth.
translations.idiomatic: Tian Bian, formerly registrar of Rongcheng, claimed skill in physiognomy and told Yanfan, "You have the bearing of a seated heavenly king, kalavinka eyes, an immortal's nose, dragon ears, and a tiger's gaze—a countenance of fierce majesty and towering fortune.

sentences.zh: 即日當乘四門輦。」

translations.literal: This very day you ought to ride the four-gate palanquin."
translations.idiomatic: Today you will ride the imperial palanquin through the four gates."

sentences.zh: 至是，有豹入其公宇，噬傷數吏，從者皆恐慄，不敢進，延範獨拔戟前逐，刺殺之，益以此自負。

translations.literal: At this time a leopard entered his official quarters, bit and wounded several clerks, and his attendants all trembled in fear and did not dare advance; Yanfan alone drew a halberd, went forward in pursuit, stabbed and killed it, and was all the more proud on this account.
translations.idiomatic: About then a leopard entered his yamen, mauled several clerks, and his attendants shrank back in terror. Yanfan alone seized a halberd, ran it down, and killed it—an exploit that swelled his pride still further.

sentences.zh: 與廣州掌務殿直趙延貴、將作監丞雷說會宿，觀天象，延貴指西方一大星曰：「此所謂『火星入南斗，天子下殿走』者也。」

translations.literal: With Zhao Yingui, a palace attendant in charge of Guangzhou affairs, and Lei Shuo, vice-director of the Directorate of Works, he lodged together and observed the heavens; Yingui pointed to a great star in the west and said, "This is what is called 'Mars enters the Southern Dipper—the Son of Heaven descends from the hall and flees.'"
translations.idiomatic: He lodged with Zhao Yingui, a Guangzhou palace attendant, and Lei Shuo of the Directorate of Works to study the night sky. Yingui pointed to a bright star in the west and said, "This is the omen 'Mars enters the Southern Dipper—the Son of Heaven flees his hall.'"

sentences.zh: 雷說出《星經》證之，乃太白行度經南斗，延貴謬為火星也。

translations.literal: Lei Shuo produced the Classic of Stars to verify it: it was Venus traversing the degrees through the Southern Dipper; Yingui had mistakenly taken it for Mars.
translations.idiomatic: Lei Shuo checked the Classic of Stars and showed it was Venus crossing the Southern Dipper—Yingui had mistaken it for Mars.

sentences.zh: 延範日夕與掌市舶陸坦議欲發兵，會坦代歸，延範寓書左拾遺韋務昇為隱語，偵朝廷機事。

translations.literal: Yanfan day and night discussed with Lu Tan, who managed the maritime trade office, a plan to raise troops; when Tan was replaced and returned, Yanfan sent a letter in cipher to the Left Reminder Wei Wusheng to spy out the court's secret affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Yanfan met daily with Lu Tan, commissioner of maritime trade, to plot raising troops. When Tan was recalled, Yanfan sent coded letters to the Left Reminder Wei Wusheng to probe the court's intentions.

sentences.zh: 延範奴視僚屬，峻刑多怨。

translations.literal: Yanfan treated his subordinates like slaves; his harsh punishments bred much resentment.
translations.idiomatic: He treated his staff like slaves and imposed harsh punishments that bred deep resentment.

sentences.zh: 會懷勇小將張霸給使轉運司，延範因事杖之，霸知延範與知廣州徐休復不協，詣休復，告延範將謀不軌及諸不法事。

translations.literal: There was the junior officer of Huaiyong, Zhang Ba, on assignment to the transport commission; Yanfan had him beaten over some matter. Ba knew Yanfan was at odds with Xu Xiufu, administrator of Guangzhou, went to Xiufu, and reported that Yanfan was plotting sedition and various unlawful acts.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Ba, a junior officer of Huaiyong serving the transport commission, was beaten by Yanfan over a petty matter. Knowing Yanfan was at odds with Guangzhou prefect Xu Xiufu, Zhang went to Xiufu and accused Yanfan of plotting rebellion and other crimes.

sentences.zh: 休復馳奏之。

translations.literal: Xiufu sent an urgent memorial reporting it.
translations.idiomatic: Xiufu sent an urgent memorial to court.

sentences.zh: 太宗遣高品閻承翰乘傳，會轉運副使李琯暨休復雜治延範，具伏。

translations.literal: Taizong sent the high-ranking Yan Chenghan by relay post to join the transport vice-commissioner Li Guan and Xiufu in jointly trying Yanfan; he confessed everything.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong dispatched the high-ranking Yan Chenghan by fast courier; together with transport vice-commissioner Li Guan and Xiufu he tried Yanfan, who confessed fully.

sentences.zh: 與昴、辨、坦俱斬廣州市，籍沒延範家。

translations.literal: Together with Mao, Bian, and Tan he was beheaded in Guangzhou city, and Yanfan's household was confiscated.
translations.idiomatic: He, together with Mao, Bian, and Tan, was executed in Guangzhou, and his family's property was confiscated.

sentences.zh: 務昇除名配商州，延貴等皆抵罪，賜霸錢十萬。

translations.literal: Wusheng was struck from the rolls and exiled to Shangzhou; Yingui and the others were all punished according to law, and Ba was granted a hundred thousand in cash.
translations.idiomatic: Wusheng was struck from the registers and exiled to Shangzhou; Yingui and the others were punished, and Zhang Ba received a reward of a hundred thousand cash.

sentences.zh: 論曰：紹斌從征討，凡逾百戰，未嘗以為憚；

translations.literal: The commentary says: Shaobin followed campaigns and punitive expeditions through more than a hundred battles and never showed fear;
translations.idiomatic: Commentary: In campaigns and punitive expeditions Shaobin fought more than a hundred battles and never showed fear;

sentences.zh: 屢被廢斥，未嘗以為慊。

translations.literal: he was repeatedly dismissed and banished, yet never showed resentment.
translations.idiomatic: though repeatedly dismissed and banished, he never bore resentment.

sentences.zh: 太祖宥盜馬罪，引見賜予，屈法使過，用能致其力也。

translations.literal: Taizu pardoned his crime of stealing horses, summoned him for audience and bestowed gifts, bent the law to let him pass his fault, and thereby was able to draw forth his strength.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu pardoned his horse-theft offense, received him in audience with gifts, bent the law to spare him, and thereby won his utmost loyalty.

sentences.zh: 榮薄事親，下詔督過。

translations.literal: Rong was neglectful in serving his parents; an edict was issued to censure his faults.
translations.idiomatic: Rong neglected his parents, and the throne issued an edict rebuking him.

sentences.zh: 瓊折州卒足以釋妖惑。

translations.literal: Qiong broke the legs of a prefectural soldier, sufficient to dispel demonic delusion.
translations.idiomatic: Qiong broke the legs of a soldier who claimed supernatural powers, thereby putting an end to the delusion.

sentences.zh: 王杲辭贐於夏。

translations.literal: Wang Gao declined gifts of tribute from Xia.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Gao refused gifts from the Xia ruler.

sentences.zh: 思鈞拔身自歸，當斬而貸。

translations.literal: Sijun escaped and returned on his own; he deserved execution yet was spared.
translations.idiomatic: Sijun escaped from captivity and returned to Song service; though liable to execution, he was spared.

sentences.zh: 琪以鄙稱。

translations.literal: Qi was known by a humble nickname.
translations.idiomatic: Qi was known by a humble sobriquet among the troops.

sentences.zh: 守俊、興輩以勇得備給使。

translations.literal: Shoujun, Xing, and their kind won appointment as attendants through valor.
translations.idiomatic: Shoujun, Xing, and men like them won palace appointments through sheer courage.

sentences.zh: 守素久練邊計，人頗畏伏。

translations.literal: Shousu had long practiced frontier strategy, and men greatly feared and submitted to him.
translations.idiomatic: Shousu had long mastered frontier strategy and was widely feared on the northern border.

sentences.zh: 重誨雖將略不足，亦有可稱。

translations.literal: Although Zhonghui's generalship was insufficient, he still had points worthy of praise.
translations.idiomatic: Though Zhonghui lacked military genius, he still had qualities worth commending.

sentences.zh: 大抵武夫悍卒，不能無過，而亦各有所長。

translations.literal: Generally speaking, martial men and fierce soldiers cannot be without faults, yet each also has his own strengths.
translations.idiomatic: In general, fierce warriors cannot avoid faults, yet each also has his own strengths.

sentences.zh: 略其過而用其長，皆足以集事。

translations.literal: Overlook their faults and employ their strengths, and all are sufficient to accomplish tasks.
translations.idiomatic: Overlook their faults and use their strengths, and each can still accomplish the state's business.

sentences.zh: 至於一勝一負，兵家常勢，顧其大節何如耳。

translations.literal: As for one victory and one defeat, these are the constant patterns of warfare; one need only consider what their great integrity is like.
translations.idiomatic: Victory and defeat are the common lot of war; what matters is the quality of a man's fundamental conduct.

sentences.zh: 若榮也，薄其所生，大節虧矣，屢以罪黜，宜哉。

translations.literal: As for one like Rong, neglectful of those who bore him, his great integrity was impaired; that he was repeatedly demoted for crimes was fitting.
translations.idiomatic: As for Rong, who neglected the parents who bore him—his fundamental conduct was flawed, and his repeated demotions were only just.
